normalised.dpsMethod: No annual (~365-day) DPS fact exists — every CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared fact is either a quarterly-rate duration or an instantaneous declaration-date fact. Annual regular DPS = sum of the four quarterly rates inside each April–March fiscal year, reconstructed from the quarterly/declaration facts and validated against divPaid/sharesBasic for every year (all agree within 0.3%). FY2020–FY2024: one declaration-date fact per year (0.135, 0.15, 0.17, 0.19 declared Apr 2019/Apr 2021/Apr 2022/Apr 2023) held for all four quarters, so DPS = 4x that rate; FY2021 has no new declaration, and divPaid/shares confirms the 0.135 rate carried unchanged. FY2025: explicit quarterly facts 0.21 (Apr–Jun 24), 0.21 (Jul–Sep 24), 0.24 (Oct–Dec 24), 0.24 (Jan–Mar 25) = 0.90 (mid-year raise). FY2026: quarterly facts 0.27 (Apr–Jun 25) and 0.27 (Jul–Sep 25) present, Q3/Q4 not yet filed; 4 x 0.27 = 1.08 confirmed by divPaid 18.021M / 16.653M shares = 1.0821. FY2017–FY2019 DPS = 0 (filed PaymentsOfDividends = 0; CSWI paid no dividend between the Sept-2015 spin-off and the Apr-2019 initiation). No split adjustment applied anywhere — CSWI has never split.

specials.note: No special dividend found. dpsAllFacts contains only regular quarterly-rate and declaration-date facts, and divPaid/sharesBasic tracks 4x the quarterly rate within 0.3% in every dividend-paying year (FY2020-FY2026), leaving no room for an unreported special. live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null, consistent with no special.

issues: DPS confidence is high: the derived annual DPS matches divPaid/sharesBasic in every dividend-paying year — FY2020 0.5406 vs 0.54, FY2021 0.5383 vs 0.54, FY2022 0.6004 vs 0.60, FY2023 0.6806 vs 0.68, FY2024 0.7600 vs 0.76, FY2025 0.8978 vs 0.90, FY2026 1.0821 vs 1.08. No year disagreed by more than 0.3%. The 'medium' overall rating is driven by the EBITDA/ROIC gaps below, not by the dividend record.

D&A JUDGEMENT CALL (material): the selected da tag is 'Depreciation' (15.907M in FY2026), not 'DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization'. For a serial acquirer that spent 1.021B on businesses in FY2026, this almost certainly excludes amortization of acquired intangibles, so every EBITDA figure here is understated and every netDebtToEbitda is overstated. FY2026 netDebt/EBITDA of 4.53x is therefore an upper bound; true leverage on a full-D&A EBITDA is likely materially lower. The DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization series (11 points, 2015-2025) was listed as a candidate but no values were provided in the file, so no correction was possible.

ROIC is null for FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 because the table carries no equity for those years — StockholdersEquity stops at 2023-03-31 and the successor tag StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest (2021-2026) has no values in the file. Per the rule, missing equity => null rather than a guess.

FY2014 and FY2015 cfo were taken from NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations (21.629M, 35.468M) because the primary NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities series only starts at FY2016. Judgement call: for FY2016 the two tags disagree (41.530M total vs 37.757M continuing) and for FY2017 continuing exceeds total (39.361M vs 39.036M), so the FY2014/FY2015 FCF figures are on a slightly different basis from later years.
FY2014 netDebt is null: no LongTermDebtNoncurrent or LongTermDebtCurrent fact exists before 2015-03-31, and treating the missing debt as zero would have invented a number.

PRE-SPIN-OFF YEARS: CSWI was separated from Capital Southwest on 2015-09-30 (inside FY2016). The FY2014/FY2015 dividends of 8.651M and 8.294M are predecessor/parent distributions, not a public dividend policy — the implied per-share figures (0.5552 and 0.5322 on 15.583M shares) are arithmetic artifacts and were deliberately EXCLUDED from the dps series, from the streak and from all CAGR windows. FY2016's 0.300M is the tail of the same pre-spin activity. Including them would fabricate a 13-year dividend history.

The dps series therefore starts at FY2017 with three genuine zero years (FY2017-FY2019, filed PaymentsOfDividends = 0). The dividend program began with the 0.135 quarterly rate declared 2019-04-04, first full year FY2020.

g10 is null: the FY2016 endpoint of the 10-year window is a zero/pre-spin year, and the rule forbids a CAGR off a zero base. gMax is measured FY2020 -> FY2026 (6 years, 12.25%/yr) from the first year of the actual dividend program; growth.fromFy reflects that, even though the dps array extends back to FY2017.

STREAK IS 5, NOT 11. priorEstimates claimed streak 11 and growth5y 19% — both are wrong. FY2021 was a HOLD at 0.54 (no declaration between Apr 2019 and Apr 2021; divPaid/shares 0.5383 vs 0.5406 confirms the flat 0.135 rate), which breaks the streak. No splits: splitFacts is empty, CSWI has never split, sharesBasic moves smoothly from 15.0M to 16.7M with no step change, and divPaid/sharesBasic reconciles to the filed quarterly rates in every year on a single basis. splitAdjustments is therefore empty and no year's DPS or share count was rescaled.

normalised.notes: CSW Industrials, March fiscal year end, so FY2026 ended 2026-03-31. The dividend program is young: initiated at 0.135/quarter declared April 2019 (FY2020), held flat through FY2021, then raised every year since — 0.54, 0.54, 0.60, 0.68, 0.76, 0.90, 1.08. Five consecutive increases, 14.9% 5-year CAGR, 16.7% over 3 years and accelerating (the FY2025 raise to 0.24 came mid-year, and a further raise to 0.30/quarter is already declared for FY2027 Q1). Coverage is very comfortable: FY2026 dividends of 18.0M against 132.4M of FCF is a 13.6% payout, 16.1% of net income; payout has never exceeded 18% of FCF in the dividend era. The one thing to watch is the FY2026 balance sheet — 1.02B of acquisitions took the company from 226M net cash to 835M net debt in a single year, and interest paid went from 4.8M to 20.9M. The 4.53x netDebt/EBITDA printed here overstates the strain because the available D&A tag captures depreciation only and omits acquisition amortization; treat it as a ceiling. No splits and no special dividends in the company's history.

issues.detail: The selected da tag is 'Depreciation' (FY2026 15.907M) rather than 'DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization'. For a filer that spent 1.021B on businesses in FY2026 (PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesGross) and grew assets from 1.379B to 2.317B, 15.9M of D&A on 17.3M of capex is plainly depreciation only, so every EBITDA is understated and every netDebtToEbitda overstated. The record discloses this, and I confirm the arithmetic is internally correct (168535+15907=184442; 835495/184442=4.5298). A complication the record did not note: the DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization candidate spans only 2015-03-31 to 2025-03-31, so switching tags would leave FY2026 with no DD&A value and force a basis break in the single most important year. Keeping Depreciation throughout is therefore the more defensible choice, but the leverage figure must be consumed as a ceiling.
issues.suggested: Keep da=Depreciation for series consistency, but re-pull DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization values (and obtain a FY2026 point) before any leverage screen uses netDebtToEbitda; until then surface latest.netDebtToEbitda 4.5298 explicitly as an upper bound, not a point estimate.

issues.detail: basis is 'summed-quarters', but only two of the four FY2026 quarterly facts exist in dpsAllFacts (0.27 for 2025-04-01/2025-06-30 and 0.27 for 2025-07-01/2025-09-30). Q3 and Q4 were inferred at 0.27 each. Derivation rule (b) requires the latest year to be marked when it is built as 4x the latest rate. The VALUE is not in dispute - divPaid 18.021M / sharesBasic 16.653M = 1.0821 independently confirms 1.08 - only the basis label misrepresents how it was derived.
issues.suggested: basis: "4x-latest-rate" (or "partial-quarters-confirmed-by-divpaid"), value unchanged at 1.08

issues.detail: basis is 'summed-quarters' for FY2020, FY2021, FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024, but none of those years has four quarterly duration facts. FY2020 rests on the instantaneous 0.135 declaration at 2019-04-04 plus one 90-day 0.135 fact; FY2022/FY2023/FY2024 rest on single instantaneous declarations (0.15 @2021-04-15, 0.17 @2022-04-14, 0.19 @2023-04-14) multiplied by four; FY2021 has no DPS fact at all and is carried forward from the 0.135 rate. The derived values are all correct (verified against divPaid/shares to within 0.24%), but 'summed-quarters' overstates the evidential basis, and FY2021 in particular is a carry-forward inference rather than any filed rate.
issues.suggested: FY2020/FY2022/FY2023/FY2024 basis: "declared-rate-x4"; FY2021 basis: "carried-rate-x4" (confirmed by divPaid/shares 0.5383). Values unchanged at 0.54/0.54/0.60/0.68/0.76.

issues.detail: basis is 'filed' for the three zero years, but no CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared fact exists for FY2017, FY2018 or FY2019 - the earliest DPS fact in dpsAllFacts is the 2019-04-04 declaration, which falls in FY2020. The zeros are inferred from PaymentsOfDividends = 0, which is a cash-flow tag, not a filed DPS tag. The zeros themselves are correct.

issues.detail: ROIC is null for all three of the most recent fiscal years, so the record supplies no usable return metric for the current period. The cause is real - StockholdersEquity in the table stops at 2023-03-31 and the table carries no equity key for 2024-03-31, 2025-03-31 or 2026-03-31 - and returning null rather than guessing is per the rule. But families.equity lists StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest with 6 points spanning 2021-03-31 to 2026-03-31, i.e. the data exists at the source and was simply not extracted into the table. This is a recoverable extraction gap, not an irreducible one, and it is the main reason the record cannot be confidence 'high'.
issues.suggested: Re-extract StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest (2021-2026) into the table and recompute ROIC for FY2024-FY2026; the FY2021-FY2023 overlap with StockholdersEquity lets you verify the two tags agree before splicing. Until then keep null.

issues.detail: FY2014 and FY2015 cfo come from NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations (21.629M, 35.468M) because the primary NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities series starts only at FY2016. The file shows the two tags are NOT interchangeable for this filer: at FY2016 they differ by 3.773M (41.530M total vs 37.757M continuing, a 9.1% gap) and at FY2017 the continuing figure EXCEEDS the total (39.361M vs 39.036M). So FY2014 FCF of 6.587M and its payoutFcf of 1.3133 sit on a different basis from FY2016 onward. The record discloses this; I confirm the magnitude of the basis gap is material at the FY2014/FY2015 FCF level.
issues.suggested: Keep the values but flag fin[2014].payoutFcf = 1.3133 as basis-inconsistent; it should not be compared to later payoutFcf figures or used in any FCF-payout trend.

issues.detail: The dps array runs FY2017-FY2026 while fin runs FY2014-FY2026, and FY2016 is dropped entirely even though PaymentsOfDividends = 0.300M for that year (implied 0.0192/share on 15.625M shares). The exclusion of FY2014/FY2015 as pre-spin parent distributions is well argued and I agree it would be wrong to present 0.5552 and 0.5322 as a dividend history. But FY2016 is treated inconsistently: it is excluded from dps while FY2017-FY2019, which are equally 'no public dividend policy' years, are included as explicit zeros. A consumer joining dps to fin on fiscal year will silently get no dps row for FY2016.
issues.suggested: Add {"fy":"2016","end":"2016-03-31","val":0,"basis":"derived-divpaid","special":null} with a note that the 0.300M is a pre-spin residual, so the dps array aligns with fin from FY2016 onward; g10 stays null either way (zero base).

issues.detail: growth.fromFy is 2020 and toFy is 2026, and gMax = 12.2462% is unambiguously a SIX-year CAGR ((1.08/0.54)^(1/6)-1 = 12.2462%, which I reproduce exactly). yearsCovered is reported as 7, which is the number of dps data points in the window, not the number of compounding periods. If any downstream consumer reads yearsCovered as N in (end/start)^(1/N), it will recompute gMax as 10.41% and disagree with the stored value.
issues.suggested: yearsCovered: 6 (compounding periods FY2020->FY2026), or rename the field to make the point-count semantics explicit.

issues.detail: The dpsMethod text and one issue string say of FY2026 that 'Q3/Q4 not yet filed', but the raw table carries a complete FY2026 row - revenue 1,082.549M, cfo 149.653M, full balance sheet at 2026-03-31, divPaid 18.021M - i.e. the FY2026 10-K is in the data. The distinction matters because 'not yet filed' implies the 1.08 figure is provisional and will firm up later, whereas in fact the year is closed and 1.08 is already confirmed by the filed full-year cash figure.
issues.suggested: Reword to: 'FY2026 is a closed, fully filed year; only the Q3/Q4 per-share RATE facts are untagged, so the 0.27 rate is carried and the 1.08 total is confirmed by filed divPaid 18.021M / 16.653M shares = 1.0821.'

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Net debt swung from -225.8M (net cash, FY2025) to +835.5M in one year on 1.021B of acquisitions; interest paid went 4.8M -> 20.9M. The 4.53x is computed on EBITDA of 184.4M built from a 'Depreciation' tag (15.9M) that plainly excludes acquired-intangible amortization, so it is a ceiling — adding a plausible 30-60M of amortization puts the true ratio at roughly 3.7x-4.2x. Above the 2.5x limit on any reading.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: Niche HVAC/plumbing/electrical consumables — sealants, brazing alloys, condensate pumps, fire-stopping — specified into codes and bought off the truck by a contractor mid-job at a few dollars a unit against a labour bill of hundreds. Brand and distributor shelf position, not price, decide the sale, and the dollar value is too small to be worth switching or for a new entrant to attack.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: FY2020 was the initiation year (0 -> 0.54) and FY2021 was a hold at 0.54, not a cut. No cut or suspension anywhere in the XBRL window; 2008 is outside the window and predates the 2015 spin-off, so there is no earlier record to test. The FY2021 hold does show management will pause the raise when leverage rises — relevant given the FY2026 balance sheet.

analysis.sectorNote: Standard industrial; no sector adjustment needed for rules 4, 7 or 8. The one model-specific read is that CSWI is a serial acquirer, which distorts two rules in opposite directions: the FCF payout of 13.6% understates how much of the cash is actually spoken for (1.02B of deals in FY2026 consumed far more than the dividend), and the 4.53x net debt/EBITDA overstates leverage because the only available D&A tag captures depreciation and omits the acquisition amortization that a serial acquirer generates. Rule 8 is therefore read as a ceiling of 4.53x with a likely true value near 3.7x-4.2x, still failing.
analysis.assessment: CSWI is an excellent business attached to a dividend that is nearly useless to an income compounder today: $4.85B market cap, 14.87% five-year DPS CAGR accelerating to 16.7% over three years, FCF compounding faster still at 18.2% — but the starting yield is 0.35%, less than a quarter of the 1.5% floor, and the payout is 13.6% of FCF rather than the 20-60% that would make the raises meaningful in cash. The snowball here is almost entirely growth, not yield: at 15% dividend growth it takes roughly twelve years for yield-on-cost to reach 2%, so the total-return case rests on the underlying compounding, not on the dividend. The thing most likely to break it is the FY2026 balance sheet — 1.021B of acquisitions flipped 225.8M of net cash into 835.5M of net debt in one year and quadrupled interest paid to 20.9M, printing 4.53x net debt/EBITDA (a ceiling; a full-D&A EBITDA is probably nearer 3.7x-4.2x), and management has already demonstrated in FY2021 that it will hold the dividend flat rather than stretch. Two prior-research figures were materially wrong and are corrected here: the streak is 5 years, not 11 (the dividend began April 2019 and FY2021 was a hold), and 5-year growth is 14.87%, not 19%. Five of ten rules pass, rules 2, 4, 5 and 8 fail and ROIC is unassessable for the three most recent years — a watch, not a buy, and worth revisiting if the leverage is worked down and the payout ratio is allowed to rise.
analysis.moat: Niche HVAC/plumbing/electrical consumables — sealants, brazing alloys, condensate pumps, fire-stopping — that a contractor pulls off the van mid-job at a few dollars against a several-hundred-dollar labour bill, so the sale is decided by code specification and distributor shelf position rather than price.
strengths: Dividend growth 14.87%/yr over 5 years and 16.67% over 3, with a further ~11% raise (0.30/qtr) already declared for FY2027 Q1
Payout of only 13.6% of FCF and 16.1% of net income — the raise can continue for a decade without touching coverage
FCF compounding at 18.2%/yr, faster than the dividend, so the payout ratio has fallen even as DPS doubled
$4.85B market cap in the ideal size band, with revenue up from 386M (FY2020) to 1,083M (FY2026)
No cut or suspension ever; no splits and no special dividends to muddy the record
risks: Yield of 0.35% is far below the usable band — the dividend contributes almost nothing to near-term total return
Leverage spiked to a ceiling of 4.53x net debt/EBITDA (likely ~3.7x-4.2x on full D&A) after 1.021B of FY2026 acquisitions; interest paid rose from 4.8M to 20.9M
Streak of only 5 years, and management already held the dividend flat once (FY2021) when leverage rose — policy is not yet proven
ROIC is unknown for FY2024-FY2026 because equity was not extracted; the FY2021 precedent shows a large deal knocks ROIC from 18.8% to 7.2%
Roll-up dependence: growth has come substantially from acquisition, so integration failure or a deal at a bad price hits both FCF and the balance sheet
FY2018 net income of -11.9M is internally implausible against 49.7M of operating income and is unverified in the source data

screenFields.streakSource: data (FY2022-FY2026); not window-limited — dividend initiated Apr 2019, FY2021 was a hold. priorEstimates.streak of 11 is rejected as impossible for a company that has only paid a dividend for 7 years.
screenFields.payoutBasis: FY2026 dividends paid 18.021M / FCF 132.396M (CFO 149.653M - capex 17.257M). On net income it is 16.08%.

estimateCorrections.why: Prior estimate was 4.13pp too high. The true FY2020->FY2026 path is 0.54 / 0.54 / 0.60 / 0.68 / 0.76 / 0.90 / 1.08; (1.08/0.54)^(1/5)-1 = 14.87%. The 19% figure likely annualised from the FY2021 base while ignoring the FY2021 hold, or extrapolated the recent 16-17% three-year rate.

Prior estimate of 11 years is not possible: CSWI only spun off from Capital Southwest on 2015-09-30 and paid nothing until the 0.135/qtr rate declared 2019-04-04. Within the dividend era FY2021 was a hold at 0.54 (divPaid/shares 0.5383 vs FY2020 0.5406, flat 0.135 rate, no declaration between Apr 2019 and Apr 2021), so strictly consecutive increases run FY2022-FY2026 only. The 11 appears to count years since the spin-off, not years of increases.

4.4pp too high — below the 5pp materiality bar but corrected because the dividend has grown more slowly than FCF since the estimate was made. FY2026 is 18.021M / 132.396M = 13.61%; 18% was last true around FY2022 (17.7%).

The dashboard carried FMP's ttmDividend of 0.96, which is exactly 4 x 0.24 — the FY2025 exit rate, a full raise-cycle stale. Filed FY2026 divPaid of 18.021M on 16.653M basic shares = 1.0821 pins the year at 4 x 0.27 = 1.08. This moves the displayed yield from 0.315% to 0.354%; the trailing-declared figure as of 2026-09-17 is 1.11 and the forward run-rate is 1.20.

stocks.m: Semi-custom rooftop HVAC and engineered data-centre cooling, specified into the job at design stage and delivered off a long-lead order book, so switching means re-engineering the mechanical design rather than changing a supplier.

normalised.dpsMethod: Filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (364-365 day duration, form 10-K, fp=FY) for every year 2009-2025, then restated to today's post-split basis. Each filed value carries the share basis of the filing it came from; basis was determined year by year from the WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesOutstandingBasic chain and cross-checked against divPaid/sharesBasic, which agrees with the filed DPS within 3.7% in every year EXCEPT FY2009 (-5.1%) and FY2010 (+51.6%). Divisors applied: FY2009-FY2010 /3.375 (three 3:2 splits still to come), FY2011 /2.25 (already restated for the 2013 split only), FY2012-FY2020 /1.5 (already restated for the 2013 and 2014 splits), FY2021-FY2025 unadjusted (already on today's basis via the Aug-2023 restatement). Quarterly/semi-annual facts were used only as corroboration, after being rebased to the split basis of the filing they came from.

splitAdjustments.note: 3:2 split, July 2013 (StockholdersEquityNoteStockSplitConversionRatio1 = 1.5 tagged 2013-05-21 / 2013-06-30 / 2013-07-02 / 2013-09-30). The FY2013 10-K restated FY2011-FY2013, so FY2011 and later already carry this split; only FY2009-FY2010 needed dividing. Evidence: sharesBasic 25.20M (2010) vs 37.03M (2011) = a 1.47x step exactly at the restatement boundary.

3:2 split, July 2014 (ratio 1.5 tagged 2014-06-05 and 2014-07-16). The FY2014 10-K restated FY2012-FY2014, so FY2012+ already carry it; FY2011 (37.03M shares = one split only) and older needed dividing. Evidence: sharesBasic 37.03M (2011) -> 55.24M (2012) -> 55.12M (2013) -> 54.81M (2014): the step is between 2011 and 2012, and 2013/2014 are flat, which is only possible if 2013 was restated for the 2014 split.

3:2 split, August 2023 (ratio 1.5 tagged 2023-08-16). The FY2023 10-K restated FY2021-FY2023, so FY2021+ are already on today's basis; FY2020 and older needed dividing. Evidence: sharesBasic 52.17M (2020) -> 78.61M (2021) = 1.507x step, and 2026 cover shares 82.45M confirms the ~81M level is today's basis.

specials.note: No separately identifiable special dividend per share could be quantified. See dataQuality for the FY2012 accelerated-payment and FY2010 cash-versus-declared analyses.

issues: CONFIDENCE IS SPLIT: the dividend/split half of this record is high confidence (17 filed annual DPS facts, split basis independently validated by a smooth today's-basis share series, divPaid/sharesBasic agreeing with filed DPS within 3.7% in 15 of 17 years); the cash-flow and leverage half is low confidence (FY2025 FCF undeterminable, capex missing for the three most recent years, no debt tag at all, EBITDA missing for four consecutive years). The single low rating reflects the weaker half.

FY2025 capex, FCF and fcfMargin are NULL, not negative. The only candidate is an unverified tagHints last-value for PaymentsToAcquireMachineryAndEquipment of 190,563,000 with no series, duration or form context, and AAON splits capital spend across at least three tags; treat 190,563,000 only as an UNVERIFIED LOWER BOUND. The prior record fcf of -190,029,000 and fcfMargin of -13.18% have been withdrawn.

FY2025 CFO is the filed NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities value of 534,000 USD versus 192,532,000 in FY2024, on net income of 107.6M, D&A of 72.3M and share-based comp of 18.0M - implying a working-capital drain near 200M in one year. Reported as filed but uncorroborated; a second, independent reason FY2025 FCF is null.

FY2023 and FY2024 capex are not derivable (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets stops at FY2022). FCF and payoutFcf are null for FY2023-FY2025, so no current-year or 5-year FCF payout or FCF growth figure is available; fcfGrowth5 is null.

Net debt and netDebt/EBITDA are null for every year: no long-term-debt tag exists in the file. Floors from DebtCurrent and cash alone: net debt >= +15,986,000 (FY2024), >= -287,000 (FY2023), >= -13,000 (FY2025). True figures are higher - InterestPaidNet is 4,817,000 (2023), 2,811,000 (2024) and 16,605,000 (2025), and total assets rose 512M in FY2025 against a 70M rise in equity. Leverage is undeterminable.

ROIC denominators omit that missing long-term debt, so FY2023-FY2025 ROIC (24.6% / 20.3% / 13.7%) is OVERSTATED, including latest.roic of 13.66%. Order-of-magnitude, ~250M of average debt in the FY2025 base would bring it to roughly 11-12%. Pre-2022 years carried essentially no interest expense, so those ROICs are close to right.

EBITDA is null for FY2018-FY2021 because the D&A family has no fact at those four year-ends. The series is NOT a mix of two D&A concepts: families.da.primary is Depreciation with 13 annual points, matching exactly the 13 year-ends carrying a da value. Any EBITDA trend line across the gap is still an interpolation.
Revenue is null for FY2009-FY2015: RevenueFromContractWithCustomerIncludingAssessedTax only starts at FY2016.
CFO for FY2013-FY2016 was taken from NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations; the two tags are identical in all four overlapping years, so the substitution is safe.
Split-basis judgement calls at FY2011 (divided by 2.25) and FY2012 (divided by 1.5) are documented in splitAdjustments and corroborated by divPaid/sharesBasic and by rebased quarterly facts.

UNRESOLVED, FY2009-FY2010 cash versus declared: cumulative cash 15,042,000 exceeds cumulative declared 12,254,000 by 2,788,000, roughly one extra 0.12 instalment. Cause not fully explained; the competing three-instalment reading of FY2010 is rejected because the same filing's nine-month cumulative is internally inconsistent with it and because the filed annual tag takes priority. dps[2010] kept at 0.0711.

FY2021 appears as a 1.3% decline (0.2533 to 0.25) largely because 0.38/1.5 = 0.2533 and post-split filings rounded the restated figure to 0.25. Underlying semi-annual rates were unchanged. cut2020 is false; FY2020-to-FY2021 is best described as flat.
g5 = 9.5683% is exact off this series but convention-sensitive at the FY2020 endpoint: on AAON's own restatement rounding (0.25) g5 would be 9.856%. Read as ~9.6-9.9%.
FY2013 shows a genuine -18.8% move in declared DPS that is a timing artifact of the accelerated December-2012 payment rather than a rate cut; the per-instalment rate rose.

The FY2024 hold (0.32 flat) is genuine: quarterly declares were 0.08 x 4 in both FY2023 and FY2024 before rising to 0.10 x 4 in FY2025. The increase streak ending at FY2025 is 1 year. AAON has had NO genuine dividend cut in the 17 years covered (yearsWithoutACut = 17).
priorEstimates (growth5y 13%, streak 11, payoutPctFcf 22%) were ignored as instructed; derived values are materially different.

normalised.notes: AAON, CIK 0000824142, December fiscal year end, 17 fiscal years of data (FY2009-FY2025). Three 3:2 stock splits (July 2013, July 2014, August 2023) were unwound year by year rather than applied blanket-fashion. The resulting today's-basis share series (87.0M in 2009 declining to 78.1M in 2019 on buybacks, then rising to 81.5M in 2025 against the 82.45M cover count) is smooth and monotonic, which independently validates the basis assignment. Regular DPS on today's basis runs 0.0711 (2009-2011, flat) to 0.4000 (2025), a 16-year CAGR of 11.4% with 3/5/10-year CAGRs of 11.3%/9.6%/10.6%. The dividend has never been genuinely cut, but it has been held flat three times (2010-2011, 2019, 2024), so the consecutive-increase streak ending at FY2025 is 1 year while the no-cut record runs the full 17 years. Net-income payout is conservative and stable at 15-42%, averaging roughly 27%. FCF payout is far less flattering than the prior 22% estimate where it can be computed at all: it exceeded 80% in 2017-2018 and exceeded 300% in 2021-2022. The dominant caveats are that capex - and therefore FCF - is not derivable for FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025, that the FY2025 CFO fact of 534,000 is uncorroborated, and that no debt tag exists at all, which makes leverage undeterminable despite 16.6M of interest paid in FY2025. REPAIR PASS: FY2025 capex/fcf/fcfMargin nulled, dpsMethod cross-check corrected to name FY2009 as well as FY2010, FY2012 quarterly-fact reasoning rewritten as corroboration on the post-split basis, FY2010 cash gap downgraded to unresolved, net-debt floors and g5 convention sensitivity added, ROIC debt-omission caveat raised to cover latest.roic, the EBITDA D&A-tag-mixing claim refuted from families.da, and confidence lowered to low.

verdicts.summary: Recomputed all 17 years of DPS, split basis, EBITDA, ROIC, FCF, growth and streak from the raw table. Dividend/split half verified exact; blocked on FY2025 FCF being published off an unverifiable single-tag capex and an implausible CFO, plus seven warns (FY2010 cash gap, FY2012 quarterly-fact reasoning, net-debt floors, EBITDA gap, g5 convention sensitivity, dpsMethod cross-check wording, confidence level). All eight were addressed in the repair pass.

Latest regular DPS 0.40 matches live ttmDividend 0.40 exactly; price-implied shares 81.91M match restated sharesBasic 81.53M (+0.47%) and the 82.45M cover count, confirming no missed split; implied yield 0.529% is consistent with AAON's long-standing sub-1% profile; g5, g3 and gMax reproduce independently. Three warns (FY2025 CFO plausibility, ROIC overstated by omitted debt, streak divergence from priorEstimates) were all folded into the repaired record.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: Live marketCap 6,189,248,052 at $75.56 (asOf 2026-09-17). Comfortably inside the cap, though above the <$5B ideal zone.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: 0.40 regular annual DPS / $75.56 = 0.529%, barely a third of the 1.5% floor. Confirmed against live ttmDividend of 0.40 with no special component (FY2025 declares were 0.10 x 4). This is a compounding-machine yield, not an income yield: at 0.53% the dividend contributes almost nothing to total return for a decade.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr split-adjusted DPS CAGR 0.2533 (FY2020) -> 0.4000 (FY2025) = 9.57%. Convention-sensitive at the FY2020 endpoint: on AAON's own restatement rounding (0.25) it is 9.86%, so read as ~9.6-9.9%. Passes but is not strong, and it is well below the 13% prior estimate. 3-yr is 11.3%, 10-yr 10.6%, 16-yr 11.4%.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.value: n/a on FCF; 30.3% of net income
rules.note: NOT ASSESSABLE ON FCF. Capex is untagged for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, so FCF and FCF payout are null for the three most recent years - including the two strongest cash years. On net income FY2025 payout is 30.3% (17-yr average ~27%), which would sit mid-band. But the last two computable FCF payouts are 343% (FY2021) and 314% (FY2022), and 84%/95% in FY2017-FY2018, because capex has repeatedly run at or above CFO. AAON is not a REIT, insurer or rate-base utility, so the NI fallback is a disclosure, not a licence to score this a pass.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: The FY2024 hold is genuine, not an artifact: quarterly declares were 0.08 x 4 in both FY2023 and FY2024 before rising to 0.10 x 4 in FY2025. The streak ending FY2025 is therefore 1 year, against a 17-year window that starts in 2009 - not window-limited, so the prior research figure of 11 cannot be substituted. The honest counterweight is yearsWithoutACut = 17: three flat years (2010-11, 2019, 2024) but no genuine cut ever.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF endpoints unavailable (FY2025 capex untagged), so assessed on net income as the rule permits: 79.009M (FY2020) -> 107.593M (FY2025) = 6.37% CAGR, 3.2pp behind the dividend. FY2025 is a depressed base - net income fell 36% from 168.6M on margin compression - so the 5-yr NI line understates the trend (FY2020->FY2024 was 20.9%/yr). Still, on the endpoints the rule specifies, the dividend outgrew earnings.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: opInc x (1 - tax/pretax) / (equity + debtCur - cash) = 13.66% for FY2025, down from 24.6% (FY2023) and 20.3% (FY2024). Two caveats pull in opposite directions: no long-term-debt tag exists, so the denominator is understated and true FY2025 ROIC is nearer 11-12% (which would fail); but FY2025 is a trough year with 512M of asset additions not yet earning. The 3-yr average of ~19% and 17-yr record (rarely below 17% before 2025) is what the business actually earns.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: No long-term-debt tag in the filing data for any of the 17 years, so netDebt is null throughout. Floors from DebtCurrent and cash alone: >= +15.99M (FY2024), >= -0.01M (FY2025). InterestPaidNet jumped from 2.8M (FY2024) to 16.6M (FY2025) and total assets rose 512M against a 70M equity rise, which proves material unreported borrowing - order-of-magnitude ~250-350M, roughly 1.2-1.6x FY2025 EBITDA of 218.5M. Likely inside 2.5x, but not evidenced.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: AAON builds semi-custom rooftop units and, via BASX, engineered data-centre cooling, configured per job rather than sold from a catalogue - so the order is won at the engineering-spec stage, months before delivery, and the backlog locks in pricing. Switching means re-speccing the mechanical design, not swapping a part number. That is a real mechanism, not price competition; the data supports it (17-yr ROIC mostly 17-30%, revenue 0.51B -> 1.44B in five years).

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: FY2020 rose 0.2133 -> 0.2533; the apparent FY2021 dip to 0.25 is split rounding (0.38/1.5 = 0.2533 vs the company's own restated 0.25) with underlying semi-annual rates unchanged - cut2020 is false. The FY2013 -18.8% move is a December-2012 accelerated payment, not a rate cut. 2008 is outside the XBRL window and is not assessed. Three flat years, zero cuts.

analysis.sectorNote: AAON is a plain Industrials manufacturer, so no sector-specific reading of the rules applies - but rules 4, 6 and 8 all had to be read off fallbacks because the filing data lacks capex for FY2023-FY2025 and lacks any long-term-debt tag for all 17 years. Rule 4 was assessed on net income (30.3%) and explicitly NOT scored a pass, since the last computable FCF payouts were 314-343%; rule 6 was assessed on net income endpoints; rule 8 was marked null rather than passed on a net-cash technicality that only exists because the debt is untagged.
analysis.moat: Semi-custom rooftop HVAC and engineered data-centre cooling, specified into the job at design stage and delivered off a long-lead order book, so switching means re-engineering the mechanical design rather than changing a supplier.
strengths: 17 fiscal years with no genuine dividend cut, including straight through 2020-2021; DPS compounded 11.4%/yr from 0.0711 to 0.40 on today's split basis.
Net-income payout is conservative and stable - 30.3% in FY2025, ~27% average over 17 years, never above 42% - so the declared dividend has structural room even in a bad year.
Return on invested capital averaged roughly 19% over the last three years and sat at 17-30% for most of the window, on a business that grew revenue from 514M (FY2020) to 1.442B (FY2025).
Market cap of $6.19B is small enough that the revenue and data-centre-cooling runway is still meaningful relative to the base.
risks: At a 0.53% yield the snowball barely starts: even 10%/yr growth takes ~21 years to reach a 4% yield on cost, so almost the entire return has to come from the share price.
FCF has repeatedly failed to cover the dividend - 84% and 95% payout in FY2017-FY2018, 343% and 314% in FY2021-FY2022 - because capex has run at or above CFO for a heavy-investment decade.

FY2025 net income fell 36% to 107.6M while the dividend rose 25%, and the reported FY2025 CFO of 534,000 (against 192.5M in FY2024) is uncorroborated; if it is even directionally right, the dividend was paid entirely out of the balance sheet last year.
Leverage is undeterminable - no debt tag in 17 years of data - while interest paid jumped from 2.8M to 16.6M and total assets rose 512M, so the balance sheet is quietly financing the expansion.
The FY2024 flat year proves the board will hold rather than stretch, so the 9.6% growth rate is a policy choice that can pause again.
analysis.assessment: AAON passes five of the ten rules and fails on the two that decide whether a dividend-growth position is worth owning today: a 0.53% starting yield (0.40 on a $75.56 price, a third of the 1.5% floor) and a one-year increase streak, since the FY2024 hold at 0.08 per quarter was genuine rather than a split artifact. What it does have is a 17-year record with no genuine cut, 9.6% five-year DPS growth, and a 30.3% net-income payout that leaves real room. The snowball here is almost all price: starting at 0.53% and compounding at ~9.6%, yield on cost reaches only about 1.3% in ten years, so you are underwriting the HVAC and data-centre-cooling franchise, not the income. The thing most likely to break it is cash coverage rather than willingness to pay - capex is untagged for FY2023-FY2025 so FCF payout cannot be computed at all, and the last two years it could be computed it was 343% and 314%, while FY2025 saw net income drop 36% to 107.6M, interest paid jump to 16.6M and reported CFO collapse to 534,000. Watch it for a materially lower price or a visible FCF-funded dividend; do not buy it for yield.

screenFields.streakSource: data; the prior research streak of 11 is contradicted - FY2023 and FY2024 both declared 0.08 x 4, a genuine flat year, and the 17-year window is not streak-limiting. Read alongside yearsWithoutACut = 17.
screenFields.payoutBasis: net income (FY2025 divPaid 32.603M / NI 107.593M). FCF payout is NOT computable for FY2023-FY2025 because capex is untagged; the last computable figures were 314% (FY2022) and 343% (FY2021).

estimateCorrections.why: 3.4pp too high. The prior figure appears to read the filed DPS series without unwinding the August 2023 3:2 split year by year. On a consistent today's-basis series the FY2020 endpoint is 0.2533, giving 9.57% (9.86% on AAON's own rounding), not 13%. The 3-year rate is 11.3% and the 16-year rate 11.4%, so 13% was never the five-year number.

FY2024 declared 0.08 per quarter, exactly matching FY2023, before rising to 0.10 per quarter in FY2025 - a genuine one-year hold that resets the consecutive-increase count. The window is 17 years and is not the binding constraint. AAON's real distinction is 17 years with no cut, not an unbroken increase streak.

Wrong on both value and basis. FCF payout cannot be computed for FY2023-FY2025 at all (no capex tag), and in the most recent computable years it was 314% (FY2022) and 343% (FY2021) - nowhere near 22%, which is not a figure this data supports in any year since FY2016. The 30.3% now shown is a net-income payout and is labelled as such in payoutBasis.

stocks.m: Smart water meters sold to municipalities on 15-year replacement cycles, where switching vendors means re-fitting a whole district's endpoints and re-integrating its billing and AMI software.

normalised.dpsMethod: Filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid (10-K, ~364-365 day duration) for FY2009-FY2011 and FY2014-FY2025. FY2012 and FY2013 have no annual fact, so they were summed from the four quarterly rate facts inside each fiscal year (2012: 0.16+0.16+0.17+0.17=0.66; 2013: 0.17+0.17+0.18+0.18=0.70), both on the pre-split basis. FY2009-FY2013 were then divided by 2 for the 2016-08-12 2:1 split; FY2014-FY2016 were already restated post-split in the filings (confirmed by sharesBasic stepping from 14.36M in 2013 to 28.61M in 2014). Every year was cross-checked against divPaid/weighted basic shares and agrees within 0.5%.

splitAdjustments.note: Single 2:1 split (StockholdersEquityNoteStockSplitConversionRatio1 = 2, 2016-08-12). Basis boundary evidence: weighted basic shares run 14.80M/14.91M/14.97M/14.33M/14.36M for FY2009-FY2013 and then step to 28.61M/28.76M/28.89M for FY2014-FY2016 - the step lands between FY2013 and FY2014, i.e. the restatement window (FY2016 10-K restating FY2015 and FY2014) already carries the post-split basis, so FY2014-FY2016 were NOT touched. divPaid/sharesBasic confirms each year internally: FY2013 = 10,004k/14,362k = 0.6966 (old basis, matches summed quarters 0.70) while FY2014 = 10,633k/28,613k = 0.3716 (matches filed 0.37). DPS for FY2009-FY2013 divided by 2; weighted basic shares for those five years multiplied by 2. Five adjusted years is consistent with a 2016 split whose filings restate only FY2014-FY2016.

specials.note: No special dividends detected. For all 17 fiscal years divPaid/weighted basic shares reproduces the split-adjusted regular DPS within 0.5% (max gap ~0.4% in FY2011 and FY2013), leaving no room for an unaccounted special distribution. live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null, consistent with this.

issues: priorEstimates (growth5y 14%, streak 33, payoutPctFcf 35%) were not used. Filed data gives a 5-yr DPS CAGR of 16.15% and an FY2025 FCF payout of 25.7%. rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: live marketCap 3,695,822,993 at $127.50 (2026-09-17). Comfortably in the ideal sub-$5B band; at 16% dividend growth the compounding runway is not capped by size.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: Latest regular annual DPS 1.48 / price 127.50 = 1.16%. Even on the FY2026 forward run-rate of 0.40 x 4 = 1.60 the yield is only 1.25%, and on the vendor TTM 1.64 it is 1.29%. All three are below the 1.5% floor. This is the single hardest constraint on BMI: the market pays 26x earnings and 4.0x sales for the growth, so the entry yield is thin.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr split-adjusted regular DPS CAGR FY2020 0.70 -> FY2025 1.48. Strong, and accelerating: 3-yr 20.30%, 10-yr 14.27%, 16-yr 12.34%. No reliance on specials - FY2025's four declared quarters (0.34+0.34+0.40+0.40) sum exactly to the annual fact.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2025 dividends 43,529k / FCF 169,672k = 25.65% (NI payout 30.7%). Industrial, so straight FCF = CFO - capex applies with no sector adjustment. Capex is light at 14.0m on 916.7m of revenue (1.5%), so FCF conversion is high and the payout has roughly 2.3x of headroom before the 60% ceiling.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy, short enough to still be fast
rules.note: The XBRL window starts FY2009 and shows 16 consecutive increases FY2010-FY2025 with no hold - the streak runs to the edge of the window, so it is window-limited. priorEstimates.streak of 33 years is plausible for Badger Meter and is what I used for the screen; at 33 years it sits just past the 30-year cap, so the rule fails on the honest figure. This is the least worrying failure in the list: the cap exists to screen out ossified slow growers, and a 33-year payer still compounding its dividend at 16.2% is not that. On the verifiable data alone (16 years) the rule would pass.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF FY2020 80,519k -> FY2025 169,672k = 16.076% against DPS 16.154% - a miss of 8 basis points, i.e. a statistical tie that is well inside the noise of a single year's working capital. The FCF payout barely moved over the five years (25.3% -> 25.7%), which is the economic test this rule is proxying. Net income compounded at 23.5% over the same period, far ahead of the dividend. Marked false because the arithmetic is what it is, but it should not be read as the dividend outrunning the business.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: Operating income x (1 - effective tax) / (equity + total debt - cash). The record used the prescribed 21% fallback because pretax income did not join FY2021-FY2025; on the derivable true effective rate of ~24.9% FY2025 ROIC is 28.3% (FY2024 38.1% rather than 40.1%). Either figure is far above the 15% strong line, and the trend is the point: 9.0% in FY2015, 17.1% in FY2020, 28.3% in FY2025.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Net cash, so it passes outright. Two caveats: no long-term-debt tag was extracted, so this is short-term borrowings minus cash and is a floor on leverage rather than a proven unlevered balance sheet; and FY2025 EBITDA inherits a depreciation figure byte-identical to FY2024, so the ratio is approximate. Even so, BMI funded 184.0m of acquisitions and 15.0m of buybacks in FY2025 and still ended the year with net cash - the direction of travel is unambiguous.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.value: Municipal replacement cycles plus installed-base software attach
rules.note: Water utilities replace meters on 15-20 year cycles under multi-year municipal contracts, and switching vendors means re-fitting an entire district's endpoints and re-integrating the billing and AMI software. The data supports the sentence rather than contradicting it: ROIC tripled to ~28% and FCF margin runs 18.5% on 10.9% revenue growth, which is not what price competition looks like.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: Raised straight through COVID, no cut, no suspension and not even a hold anywhere in the FY2009-FY2025 window. 2008 sits outside the XBRL window so it cannot be checked here.

analysis.assessment: Badger Meter is an excellent business at an uncomfortable entry price: $3.70B market cap, 28.3% ROIC, net cash of $226M and 16 straight years of increases in the filed data, but a regular yield of just 1.16% on $1.48 of FY2025 dividends at $127.50. The snowball is entirely growth-driven rather than yield-driven - 16.2% five-year DPS growth (accelerating to 20.3% over three years) against a 25.7% FCF payout means the dividend could roughly double from payout expansion alone before touching the 60% ceiling, so a buyer today is underwriting about a decade of 15%+ raises to reach a 4-5% yield on cost. Coverage is not the constraint: FCF of $169.7M covers the $43.5M dividend 3.9x, capex is 1.5% of revenue, and net income compounded at 23.5% over five years while the dividend compounded at 16.2%, so the payout ratio fell even as the dividend more than doubled. The two failed rules are soft - the 33-year streak fails only by being eight years past the 30-year cap, and rule 6 misses by 8 basis points on FCF growth that is a tie in all but the last decimal. What most likely breaks it is the price, not the company: at 26x earnings and 4.0x sales there is no yield cushion, so a stall in the municipal AMI replacement cycle or digestion trouble in the $184M of FY2025 acquisitions would hit the share price hard while paying you 1.2% to wait.

Rule 4 uses straight FCF (CFO - capex) with capex at 1.5% of revenue; rule 8's net-cash reading is sound in direction but rests on a net-debt series that can only see short-term borrowings, so it is a floor on leverage rather than proof of zero term debt.

issues.detail: windowLimited is set to false, which is literally defensible (the streak starts at FY2010, two years inside the FY2008 data boundary). But the record's own issues argue the FY2009 'hold' at 0.25 is a declaration-timing artefact (quarterly declared rate rose 0.12 -> 0.13 during fiscal 2009, quarterly facts sum to ~0.51 vs a filed annual 0.50). If that is right, the increase run reaches the first year in data and the streak IS window-limited - and the true record is the 30-plus years external sources (and priorEstimates' 33) report. As published, a downstream consumer reading windowLimited=false will treat 16 as a complete, bounded streak for a company that is in fact a multi-decade dividend grower.

issues.detail: The record knowingly departs from the stated derivation rule ('fiscal-year label = calendar year of the period END date') for six periods: 2009-01-03, 2010-01-02, 2011-01-01, 2015-01-03 and 2016-01-02 are pushed back one calendar year. I did not raise it to a block because the literal rule is degenerate for a 52/53-week filer: it collides 2011-01-01 with 2011-12-31 and 2016-01-02 with 2016-12-31, silently destroying two fiscal years and creating a phantom gap. The record's mapping is one-to-one, monotonic and matches how FELE itself labels these years. Downstream consumers must be aware that g10 uses the period ending 2016-01-02 as the FY2015 endpoint, not the period ending 2016-12-31.

issues.detail: The stated cause of the persistent +0.3% to +5.6% gap between divPaid/sharesBasic and filed DPS is 'PaymentsOfDividends including dividends to noncontrolling interests'. That is weakly supported by this file: PaymentsToMinorityShareholders is a separate tag whose last value is 0, and there is no NCI dividend line in the table. A more likely driver is that WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesOutstandingBasic excludes unvested participating restricted shares that nonetheless receive cash dividends, plus declared-vs-paid timing. The CONCLUSION (no special dividends) is correct and independently confirmed: the gap is one-directional with divPaid/shares ABOVE DPS in every year, which is the opposite of the special-dividend signature, and no year shows a non-recurring divPaid spike. Only the explanatory attribution is unsupported.

This is the conservative choice and is defensible, but it is a different treatment from FY2008/FY2009, where the nulls are genuinely forced by missing data. The asymmetry should be flagged rather than presented as one uniform rule.
issues.suggested: Either keep null and state explicitly 'FY2010 nulled by choice because debtLT values were not supplied despite the tag existing', or note the bound: with debtLT unknown, net debt at 2011-01-01 is at most 1,241,000 - 140,070,000 = -138,829,000 plus unknown long-term debt, i.e. FELE was near net cash.

issues.detail: Confidence is 'high' while 6 of 18 DPS observations (FY2020-FY2025, one third of the series, including the latest year and both the g3 and g5 endpoints) rest on an INFERRED Q4 rate that appears in no filed fact, and the fiscal-year labelling required a documented departure from the stated rule. The inference is well-evidenced (Q1-Q3 rates identical, 272/273-day cumulative exactly 3x the rate, FMP TTM 1.105 corroborating the 0.265 Q4) and I could not refute it, but 'high' overstates the standing of a series whose most recent third is partly constructed.
issues.suggested: confidence = 'medium-high', or keep 'high' and add the qualifier 'high for FY2008-FY2019 filed facts; FY2020-FY2025 depend on an inferred but corroborated Q4 rate'.

issues.detail: The series mixes two economically different tags without marking it per year: FY2008-FY2011 use CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared while FY2012 onward use CashPaid. This matters at exactly the point the record identifies as the streak break: the FY2009 'hold' at 0.50 declared is a declared-basis artefact - the fiscal-2009 quarterly declared facts imply 0.12 + 0.13 + 0.13 + 0.13 = 0.51, i.e. the rate actually rose mid-year. The record says so in dataQuality but the basis field still reads 'split-adjusted' rather than flagging the tag change, so a downstream reader could take the 16-year streak as a hard ceiling.
issues.suggested: Add basis detail 'split-adjusted (declared)' for FY2008-FY2010 and 'filed (declared)' for FY2011, so the FY2009 hold is visibly tag-driven; keep values unchanged (0.25 / 0.25 / 0.26 / 0.2675) since rule (a) mandates the filed annual fact.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: Live market cap 4,248,721,594 at $96.10 on 2026-09-17. Inside the ideal sub-$5B band; ~44.2M shares implied, still shrinking (165.6M repurchased in FY2025).

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: Latest regular annual DPS 1.06 / price 96.10 = 1.10%. On the forward run-rate (0.28 x 4 = 1.12) it is 1.17%, and TTM 1.105 gives 1.15% - all well below the 1.5% floor. This is the rule FELE fails hardest: you are buying growth, not income.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr DPS CAGR 0.62 (FY2020) -> 1.06 (FY2025). 3-yr 10.77%, 10-yr 10.73%, 17-yr 8.87%. Just short of the 12% 'strong' mark; the FY2026 Q1 raise to 0.28 is +5.7%, a visible deceleration.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2025 dividends 50.0M / FCF 193.5M = 25.8%; on net income 34.0%. Mid-band with roughly 2.3x of headroom before the 60% ceiling. Only FY2014 (147%) ever breached it, on a one-off weak CFO.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: 16 consecutive increases in the XBRL window, which begins FY2008 - the streak does not reach the window edge, so it is not window-limited and the data figure is used. The FY2009 flat year is a declared-vs-paid artefact (quarterly declared rate rose 0.12 -> 0.13 mid-year), so the real record is almost certainly the ~33 years prior research claims; either way the rule passes on the data streak.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF endpoints are erratic (189.0M in FY2020 on an exceptional working-capital release, 59.8M in FY2022, 274.3M in FY2023, 193.5M in FY2025), so net income is the fairer read: 100.5M -> 147.1M = 7.92%/yr, still below the 11.32% dividend CAGR. The dividend has been growing partly by expanding the payout (15.7% -> 25.8% of FCF), which is sustainable for a while but not indefinitely.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 NOPAT 205.5M on invested capital 1,389.9M. Ten straight years above 9%, peaking at 17.3% in FY2023; FY2025 dips on a higher 23.6% effective tax rate and the 114.7M acquisition adding capital.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Net debt 67.3M against EBITDA 331.9M. FELE was in net cash in FY2020 (-36.3M) and FY2024 (-91.1M); leverage has never exceeded 1.11x in the window.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: Groundwater and fuel-system pumps are sold through a fragmented network of local well drillers and fuel-station contractors who stock and specify what they know; replacement is emergency-driven and the pump is a small fraction of total job cost, so the installed base and distributor relationships, not price, decide the sale.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: DPS rose 0.58 -> 0.62 -> 0.70 straight through COVID. 2008 is outside the XBRL window (coverage starts FY2008 only for the annual fact), so the GFC behaviour cannot be verified from this data.

analysis.assessment: FELE passes eight of ten rules and is a textbook small-cap compounder: $4.25B market cap, 14.8% ROIC, 0.20x net debt/EBITDA, and a 16-year run of increases compounding at 11.3% over five years. The snowball is all growth and no income - a 1.10% starting yield on $96.10 means roughly nine years of 11% raises before the yield on cost even reaches today's S&P average, and a 25.8% FCF payout gives management plenty of runway to keep raising. The catch is rule 6: FCF has gone nowhere over five years (+0.5%/yr) and net income only +7.9%/yr, so a meaningful slice of the dividend growth has come from expanding the payout rather than from the business, and the FY2026 Q1 raise of just 5.7% (0.265 -> 0.28) looks like management already acknowledging that. FY2025 is the warning shot: revenue up to $2.13B and EBITDA up to $331.9M, but net income down 18% to $147.1M on a 23.6% tax rate, pushing payout-on-earnings to 34%. The thing most likely to break it is not the balance sheet, it is earnings stalling around $2B of revenue while the dividend keeps compounding double-digit - at which point the raises converge on mid-single digits and the low starting yield never gets rescued.
analysis.moat: Groundwater and fuel pumping systems sold through a fragmented network of local drillers and fuel contractors who specify from habit, where emergency replacement and a large installed base - not price - decide the order.
strengths: Ideal size: $4.25B cap, well inside the sub-$5B sweet spot, with a shrinking share count (46.4M weighted basic in FY2019 to 45.0M in FY2025).
Payout runway: 25.8% of FCF and 34.0% of a tax-depressed net income; only one breach (FY2014) in eighteen years.
Fortress balance sheet: 0.20x net debt/EBITDA, net cash in two of the last six years, never above 1.11x in the window.
Consistent capital returns: ROIC above 12% in nine of the last ten years, peaking at 17.3% in FY2023.
Dividend raised straight through COVID (+6.9% FY2020, +12.9% FY2021) with no cut or hold since FY2009.
risks: Starting yield of 1.10% is far below the 1.5% floor - the total-return case depends almost entirely on price and growth, not income.
5-yr FCF CAGR of 0.48% and net income CAGR of 7.9% both lag the 11.3% dividend CAGR; growth has been part-funded by payout expansion.
FY2026 Q1 raise of 5.7% (0.265 -> 0.28) is roughly half the trailing 5-year pace - the fastest-visible signal that the growth rule may stop passing.
FY2025 net income fell 18% to $147.1M despite record revenue and EBITDA, on a 23.6% effective tax rate and a $114.7M acquisition; the record asserts 'tax-depressed' without a fuller bridge.
Revenue has been flat at roughly $2.0-2.1B for four years (FY2022-FY2025), so the earnings engine behind the dividend is not currently compounding.
FCF is structurally lumpy ($59.8M FY2022 to $274.3M FY2023), so any single-year payout ratio understates the real volatility of coverage.
analysis.sectorNote: Franklin Electric is a straightforward Industrials manufacturer, so all ten rules apply as written - no REIT, insurer or regulated-utility adjustment is needed. Rule 4 is on FCF (CFO minus PP&E capex, acquisitions excluded as growth capital) and rule 6 was additionally read on net income because FCF endpoints are erratic, as the rule permits.

screenFields.streakSource: data (16 consecutive increases FY2010-FY2025; not window-limited, XBRL starts FY2008). Prior research claims 33 years and is likely right - the FY2009 flat year is a declared-basis timing artefact - but it cannot be confirmed from filings, so the data streak is used.
screenFields.payoutBasis: FCF (FY2025 dividends 50.0M / FCF 193.5M); on net income 34.0%

estimateCorrections.why: Prior research claimed 33 years. XBRL coverage begins at fiscal 2008, so only 16 consecutive increases (FY2010-FY2025) are verifiable; the FY2009 flat year at 0.25 is a declared-vs-paid timing artefact rather than a real hold, so the true streak is probably longer than 16 but cannot be evidenced from filings. Screen now shows the verifiable 16.

Actual 5-yr DPS CAGR is 11.32% (0.62 FY2020 -> 1.06 FY2025), 2.3pp above the prior 9% estimate - below the 3pp materiality bar but corrected for accuracy. Note the forward pace is slowing: the FY2026 Q1 raise is only 5.7%.
FY2025 dividends 50.0M / FCF 193.5M = 25.8%, 4.2pp below the prior 30% estimate - inside the 5pp bar but corrected. On net income the figure is 34.0%.

stocks.m: Municipal and industrial pumps written into wastewater and fire-protection specifications, with a decades-long installed base that routes replacement parts and drop-in units back to the original maker because requalifying a pump station is an engineering project.

normalised.dpsMethod: Regular annual DPS built from the quarterly CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid rate facts, chained year-to-year and validated against divPaid/weighted-basic-shares for every year 2011-2025 (agreement <=0.08% in all years except FY2018, where the gap is the special dividend). Filed FY annual facts (2009, 2010, 2011, 2013, 2014, 2020) were used where they agree with that cross-check; FY2009 and FY2010 filed values were divided by 1.25 for the 5:4 split (they are the only two years still on the old basis); FY2012's filed annual fact (0.283) is a stale duplicate of FY2011 and was replaced by the derived 0.312; FY2018's filed 2.51 includes a $2.00 special, so regular 0.51 was taken from PaymentsOfOrdinaryDividends/shares and the quarterly chain; FY2021's filed 0.64 is a rounded presentation of the actual 0.635.

splitAdjustments.note: 5-for-4 split effective between the Q3-2012 10-Q (Nov 2012) and the FY2012 10-K. splitFacts is empty, so the date is inferred: CommonStockSharesOutstanding steps 20,990,893 (2011-12-31) -> 26,246,116 (2012-12-31), a 1.2504x step, and WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesOutstandingBasic 2011 (26,234,579) is exactly 1.25x WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding 2011 (20,987,663), i.e. basic was restated and diluted was not. Only FY2009 and FY2010 remain on the old basis in this dataset: their filed annual DPS (0.324, 0.336) equals 4x their own pre-split quarterly rate of 0.084 and sits ABOVE FY2011/FY2013 on an otherwise smooth rising trend. FY2011 and FY2012 are ALREADY post-split (FY2011 filed 0.283 = divPaid/basic 0.28321; FY2012 derived 0.312 = divPaid/basic 0.31201), so they were NOT divided. Two years adjusted, consistent with a restatement window that reached FY2011-FY2012 while the originally-filed FY2010 and FY2009 facts survived untouched in the extraction. Shares: no basic-share fact exists for 2009-2010 so no share multiplication was needed; for reference CommonStockSharesOutstanding 2010 (20,985,668) and 2011 (20,990,893) are old-basis and would be 26,232,085 / 26,238,616 on today's basis.

specials.note: FY2018 only. Filed CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid FY2018 = 2.51 vs a regular quarterly chain of 0.125+0.125+0.125+0.135 = 0.51. DividendsCommonStockCash 2018 = 65,551,000 while PaymentsOfOrdinaryDividends 2018 = 13,317,000; the 52,234,000 difference over 26,112,138 basic shares = 2.0004, i.e. a $2.00/share special paid in 2018. Regular 0.51 = 13,317,000/26,112,138 = 0.51001, confirming the split of the two components. No other year shows a filed DPS above divPaid/shares. live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null and live.ttmDividend 0.76 = 4 x the current 0.19 regular rate, so no special sits in the TTM.

normalised.notes: GRC, Dec FYE, so FY label = calendar year of period end. Regular DPS rises in every single year 2010-2025 (16 consecutive increases inside the data window); GRC's real streak predates 2009, so windowLimited is true and the 53-year prior estimate is not contradicted by this data. The quarterly chain is internally perfect: the annual raise lands on the Q4 payment and the new rate carries into Q1-Q3 of the next year (e.g. FY2023 Q4 0.18 = FY2024 Q1-Q3 0.18), which let every missing Q4 be pinned by the following January rate and then independently confirmed by divPaid/sharesBasic. 5-yr regular DPS CAGR is 4.78%/yr and 3-yr is 2.84%/yr, i.e. growth is decelerating and the 5% prior estimate is optimistic on the 3-yr view. Payout on FCF at FY2025 is 22.1%, well below the 35% prior estimate, because FY2025 FCF (88.9m) was a record; the 5-yr average payoutFcf is nearer 30%. The balance sheet changed character in FY2022 with the debt-funded Fill-Rite acquisition: net debt went from -125m (net cash) at FY2021 to +430m at FY2022, and has been paid down to 272m (2.21x EBITDA) by FY2025. FY2022 is the only negative-FCF year in the window (CFO collapsed to 13.7m), so payoutFcf is null there.

issues: SPLIT JUDGEMENT: splitFacts is empty, so both the 5:4 ratio and the 2012 timing are inferred, not filed. Ratio evidence: sharesBasic 2011 (26,234,579) / sharesDil 2011 (20,987,663) = 1.2500 exactly, and sharesOut steps 20,990,893 -> 26,246,116 between 2011-12-31 and 2012-12-31. Timing evidence: the 2012 Q1-Q3 quarterly DPS facts (0.09/0.10/0.10) are old basis while the 2013 Q1 fact (0.08 = 0.10/1.25) is new basis, so the split fell between Nov 2012 and the FY2012 10-K.

SPLIT SCOPE: only FY2009 and FY2010 were divided by 1.25. FY2011 and FY2012 are already post-split in this dataset (FY2011 filed 0.283 = divPaid/basic 0.28321; FY2012 derived 0.312 = divPaid/basic 0.31201), so dividing them would have double-adjusted. This is a narrower window than the usual 'split year plus two prior years' rule would suggest - the extraction kept the originally-filed FY2010 fact (0.336 = 4 x the old-basis 0.084 quarterly rate) rather than any restated version. The trend test is decisive: leaving FY2010 at 0.336 would put it above both FY2011 (0.283) and FY2013 (0.33) on an otherwise monotonically rising series.
SPLIT DATE recorded as '2012' rather than an exact day, because no split fact exists in the source and no filing dates are available to narrow it further.

FY2012 FILED DPS IS WRONG: CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid for 2012-01-01/2012-12-31 (10-K, FY) = 0.283, an exact duplicate of the FY2011 value. It is contradicted by that year's own 9-month cumulative quarterly fact (0.29 old basis = 0.232 new basis) - an annual figure cannot be below its own 9-month cumulative - and by divPaid/sharesBasic = 0.31201. The derived 0.312 was used instead of the filed tag.

FY2021 FILED DPS IS ROUNDED: filed FY2021 = 0.64, but divPaid/sharesBasic = 0.63501 and the quarterly chain gives 0.155x3 + 0.17 = 0.635 (the 0.17 Q4 rate is confirmed by the 2022 Q1-Q3 facts of 0.17). 0.635 was used; the -0.8% disagreement with the filed tag is the only case where a filed annual value was overridden purely for rounding.

FY2018 CROSS-CHECK DISAGREES BY 392% - this is the special dividend, separated into 0.51 regular + 2.00 special. payoutNi (1.64) and payoutFcf (2.17) for FY2018 are computed on total divPaid per the schema and are not comparable to other years; regular-only payoutFcf for FY2018 is 0.44.
FY2015 cross-check off by -0.08% (implied 0.40466 vs 0.405) and FY2023 by -0.03% (0.70478 vs 0.705); both are within payment-date/share-count timing noise, no adjustment made.

CAPEX TAG SWITCH: the primary family PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets starts at FY2013. FY2009-FY2012 capex was taken from PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment (38,071k / 8,310k / 11,175k / 16,373k), named per-year in capexTag. The two tags overlap in 2013 (21,014 vs 21,015) and 2014 (13,278 vs 13,275), confirming they are the same line. FY2010's separate PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesAndInterestInAffiliates of 33,856k was deliberately excluded from capex as acquisition spend.

FY2009 capex of 38,071k is 4.6x the FY2010 figure and drives an anomalously low FY2009 FCF (11,657k). It is the value as tagged and no adjustment was made, but FY2009 FCF and payoutFcf should be treated as suspect.

DEBT ASSUMED ZERO PRE-2021: LongTermDebtNoncurrent/LongTermDebtCurrent exist only for FY2021-FY2025 (both 0 at FY2021). For FY2009-FY2020 netDebt was computed as -cash. This is an assumption, not filed data. It is supported by tagged interest expense of 1k-179k per year over that span and by the explicit 0/0 debt at FY2021, but any small borrowings in 2009-2020 are omitted. The same assumption flows into the ROIC denominator for those years.

sharesBasic (WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesOutstandingBasic) is not filed for FY2009 or FY2010, so those years are null. No divPaid/shares cross-check was possible for 2009-2010; their share basis was established from the quarterly rate facts and the trend test instead.

sharesDil FY2009 is 20,886,309,000 in the source - a 1000x units error (should be ~20,886,309). Not used, but it means the diluted-share family is unreliable. Separately, sharesDil for FY2011/FY2012 (~20.99m) is stale pre-split while sharesBasic for the same years is restated post-split - a useful signal, but a trap if the diluted series were used for per-share work.

pretax (IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxes...) is missing for FY2009 and FY2010, so the effective tax rate for those years was derived as tax/(netIncome+tax) = 32.97% and 32.27% rather than the 21% fallback, which would have badly overstated after-tax operating profit for that era.
equity is not filed for FY2009 (StockholdersEquity starts 2010-12-31), so FY2009 ROIC is null per the rule.

FY2022 opIncome (40,183k) sits far above pretax (13,872k) because of acquisition financing and purchase-accounting charges; the resulting FY2022 ROIC of 4.3% and EBITDA of 61.3m reflect the tagged figures as filed and are not comparable to adjacent years.
FY2022 FCF is negative (-4,301k) so payoutFcf is null for that year by rule; netDebtToEbitda of 7.01x that year is real but flattered downward in later years by the EBITDA step-up.

divPaid signs are inconsistent in the source (negative for FY2009-FY2012, positive from FY2013); absolute values were used throughout. DividendsCommonStockCash and PaymentsOfOrdinaryDividends agree exactly in every overlapping year except FY2018, where the difference is precisely the special.
priorEstimates were ignored as instructed. For the record they were materially off: 35% payoutFcf vs 22.1% actual at FY2025, and 5% growth vs 4.78% 5-yr / 2.84% 3-yr actual.

issues.detail: The derivation rule states "Effective tax = tax / pretax (fallback 21%)". pretax is absent for FY2009 and FY2010, so the rule mandates the 21% fallback, but the record used a substituted rate of tax/(netIncome+tax) = 32.27% for FY2010. That single choice moves FY2010 ROIC by ~17% relative. FY2009 is unaffected because its ROIC is null on missing equity. The substitute rate is arguably the better estimate and is disclosed in issues, but it is a departure from the stated method and the record does not present the rule-literal alternative.

issues.detail: Derivation rule (a) says a filed annual DPS tag with ~1-year duration should be used. A filed FY2021 fact exists (0.64, 10-K, 364 days) and the record overrode it with 0.635 purely on a rounding argument, a -0.78% change. The override is well-evidenced (divPaid/basic = 0.63501; quarterly chain 0.155x3 + 0.17 with the 0.17 confirmed by the 2022 Q1-Q3 facts) and does not affect g3/g5/g10 or the streak, but it is the one place where a compliant filed value was discarded.
issues.suggested: Keep 0.635 but flag basis as "filed-overridden-rounding" rather than "summed-quarters", so the deviation from rule (a) is visible in the data rather than only in prose.

issues.detail: yearsCovered is 17, which is the count of fiscal-year data points (2009-2025 inclusive), while gMax 6.8212% is computed over 16 year-spans (2009 to 2025). A consumer reading yearsCovered as the gMax horizon would recompute (0.745/0.2592)^(1/17)-1 = 6.39% and see a 0.43pp mismatch. The field is ambiguous rather than wrong.
issues.suggested: Either rename/redefine to yearsCovered = 16 (the CAGR horizon, consistent with gMax) or add an explicit gMaxYears: 16.

issues.detail: "high" is generous given the stack of judgement calls the record itself lists: splitFacts is empty so both the 5:4 ratio and the 2012 timing are inferred; the split scope deliberately departs from the two-year restatement window; debt is ASSUMED zero for FY2009-FY2020 (which flows into netDebt, netDebtToEbitda and the ROIC denominator for twelve of seventeen years); revenue is null for seven years; the filed FY2012 DPS is discarded as corrupt; and the two most recent DPS years have no supporting quarterly facts. Each call is individually defensible and the cross-checks are tight, but the aggregate is not a high-confidence extraction.
issues.suggested: Downgrade confidence to "medium", with the split-basis inference, the pre-2021 zero-debt assumption and the unobservable FY2024-FY2025 quarterly chain named as the three drivers.

issues.detail: The note offers the sharesOut step 20,990,893 (2011-12-31) -> 26,246,116 (2012-12-31) as ratio evidence. That step is not a clean split signal: sharesOut for 2011 is an un-restated old-basis instant fact sitting alongside a restated post-split sharesBasic for the same year, so the 1.2504x "step" is an artefact of mixing bases, not a measured split ratio, and it disagrees with the true ratio in the fourth digit. The decisive evidence is elsewhere in the same note (sharesBasic2011/sharesDil2011 = 1.250000 exactly, and the 0.10 -> 0.08 quarterly rate break between 2012 Q3 and 2013 Q1), so the conclusion stands.
issues.suggested: Demote the sharesOut step to corroboration and lead with the exact 1.250000 basic/diluted ratio and the 2012Q3 0.10 -> 2013Q1 0.08 quarterly rate break as the ratio and timing evidence.

issues.detail: payoutNi 1.6396 and payoutFcf 2.1660 are computed on total divPaid of 65,551,000, which includes the $2.00/share special (52,234,000). They are arithmetically correct per the schema and the record flags them, but they are the only two payout figures in the series that are not regular-dividend payouts, and any downstream 5-year or 10-year average payout that includes FY2018 will be badly distorted. The regular-only figures are payoutFcf 13,317/30,263 = 0.4400 and payoutNi 13,317/39,979 = 0.3331.
issues.suggested: Add explicit regular-only companions for FY2018 (payoutFcfRegular 0.44, payoutNiRegular 0.3331) so averaging consumers cannot silently pick up the special.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: live marketCap 1,906,024,134 at $72.17 (2026-09-17). Well inside the ideal band - a 26.4m-share, ~$682m-revenue pump maker.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: FY2025 regular DPS 0.745 / 72.17 = 1.03%; on the current 0.19/qtr run rate (0.76 annual) it is 1.05%. No special in the TTM. Roughly 45bp short of the band's floor - the single biggest structural objection.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr regular DPS CAGR 0.59 -> 0.745 = 4.78%/yr, and decelerating: 3-yr 2.84%, 10-yr 6.28%, 16-yr 6.82%. Raises have been a flat ~$0.005/qtr step since 2022, i.e. the growth rate mechanically shrinks each year.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2025 dividends 19.6m / FCF 88.9m (CFO 106.2m - capex 17.4m) = 22.1%; 5-yr average (ex the null FY2022) is 32.5%. On net income it is 36.9%. Sits at the low end of the band, with FY2025 FCF a record - normalised FCF nearer 55-60m would put payout around 33%.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy, short enough to still be fast
rules.note: The XBRL window shows 16 consecutive increases (2010-2025) and reaches the 2009 start, so it is window-limited; prior research puts the true streak at 53 years, which the data does not contradict. 53 years clears the 10-year floor decisively but breaks the 30-year ceiling - this is a Dividend King whose policy is proven and whose raises are now ceremonial rather than fast.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF 43.2m (FY2020) -> 88.9m (FY2025) = 15.5%/yr, helped by the Fill-Rite acquisition lifting EBITDA from 48m to 123m. Net income also outgrew the dividend (25.2m -> 53.0m, 16.0%/yr). Both endpoints are positive so no net-income substitution was needed.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 op income x (1 - effective tax) / (equity + total debt - cash) = 10.6%; 5-yr average 10.7%. GRC earned 13-15% pre-2022 on a net-cash balance sheet; the debt-funded Fill-Rite deal added roughly $380m of invested capital and ROIC has only climbed back from 4.3% (FY2022) to 10.6%. It has not yet earned back its acquisition price.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Net debt 272.4m / EBITDA 123.1m = 2.21x, down from 7.01x at the FY2022 deal close and 2.87x at FY2024 - roughly 35-70m of paydown a year. Passes now, but this was a net-cash company (-125m) as recently as FY2021 and debt still has first claim on cash flow.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: Gorman-Rupp pumps are written into municipal wastewater and fire-protection specifications and sit in service for decades; replacement parts and drop-in replacements flow to the original maker because requalifying a pump means re-engineering the station. Fill-Rite adds a branded fuel-transfer aftermarket on the same logic. Real, but it defends share rather than pricing power - which is exactly why growth is 3-5% and not 8%.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: FY2020 DPS 0.59 vs 0.55, FY2021 0.635 vs 0.59 - raised straight through COVID, and raised again in FY2022 while taking on 430m of acquisition debt. No cut or hold anywhere in the 2009-2025 window. 2008 sits outside the XBRL window and is not assessed here.

analysis.assessment: Gorman-Rupp is a proven dividend payer priced as one: a $1.91B pump maker yielding 1.03% on FY2025 regular DPS of $0.745 (1.05% on the current $0.19/qtr rate), with a 53-year raise streak that the 2009-2025 data confirms for 16 unbroken years. The payout is genuinely safe - 19.6m of dividends against 88.9m of FY2025 FCF is 22.1%, and 32.5% on the five-year average - so the runway is not the problem; the problem is that management converts that runway into a flat $0.005/quarter raise, which is 4.78% over five years and only 2.84% over three, and mechanically decays further each year. The snowball here is a slow one: 1.0% yield compounding at under 5% does not double your income inside a decade, and the total-return case rests on the Fill-Rite integration, where ROIC is still only 10.6% against 13-15% pre-deal and net debt of 272m (2.21x EBITDA) is absorbing 35-70m a year that used to be dry powder. The most likely thing to break it is not a cut - it is permanence of the current pattern: if raises stay at half a cent a quarter while municipal capex normalises from the FY2023-25 revenue surge (378m to 682m), the dividend grows below inflation and the position becomes a bond with equity risk. Buy it for the durability of the spec-in installed base, not for income growth.
analysis.moat: Municipal and industrial pumps written into wastewater and fire-protection specifications, with a decades-long installed base that routes replacement parts and drop-in units back to the original maker because requalifying a pump station is an engineering project.
strengths: Payout at 22.1% of FY2025 FCF (32.5% five-year average) leaves the dividend covered roughly 4.5x - there is no coverage risk at any plausible earnings level.
Raised the dividend through COVID and through the leveraged FY2022 Fill-Rite acquisition; 16 unbroken increases in the data, 53 by prior research.
FCF compounded 15.5%/yr over five years (43.2m to 88.9m) versus 4.78% dividend growth - earnings are outrunning the payout, not chasing it.
Deleveraging is real and fast: net debt 430m (7.01x) at FY2022 to 272m (2.21x) at FY2025, with FY2025 FCF of 88.9m against 19.6m of dividends.
$1.91B market cap on ~$682m of revenue - small enough that incremental municipal and fuel-transfer wins still move the numbers.
risks: Yield of 1.03% is roughly 45bp below the usable band; at 4.78% growth it takes about 9 years just to reach a 1.5% yield on cost.
Dividend growth is decelerating on a fixed half-cent-per-quarter raise policy: 6.28% (10-yr) to 4.78% (5-yr) to 2.84% (3-yr).
ROIC of 10.6% is below the 12% bar and below GRC's own 13-15% pre-acquisition level - the Fill-Rite purchase has not yet paid for itself.
Revenue jumped 378m (FY2021) to 682m (FY2025) largely on acquisition plus a municipal capex cycle; a normalisation would expose the 2.21x leverage.
FY2022 is a live reminder of fragility in the model: CFO collapsed to 13.7m, FCF went to -4.3m and net income to 11.2m in a single acquisition year.
A 53-year streak creates its own trap - management will defend a token raise long after growth stops justifying the holding.
analysis.sectorNote: Standard industrial manufacturer, so all ten rules apply as written with no sector substitution: rule 4 uses dividends / (CFO - capex) and rule 8 uses reported net debt / EBITDA. The one contextual read is rule 5 - the 10-30 year band is designed to catch companies young enough to still be accelerating, and a 53-year Dividend King fails it on the ceiling, not on the floor. That failure is a statement about future growth rate, not about dividend safety.
