rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: Live market cap 10,006,596,630 at $86.33 (2026-09-17). Passes but is not in the ideal sub-$5B band, so the size tailwind is moderate.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: 1.14 FY2025 regular DPS / $86.33 = 1.32%. Even on the FMP ttm of 1.24 it is only 1.44%, and on the >=1.20 FY2026 run-rate 1.39%. Below the band on every basis - you are buying growth, not income.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 0.84 (FY2020) -> 1.14 (FY2025). Misses the bar, though the trend is improving: 3-yr CAGR is 8.20% (0.90 -> 1.14) and the FY2026 raise to a 0.30 quarterly rate is another ~5-6%. 10-yr is only 5.46%.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2025 dividends 131.9M / FCF 339.9M. Comfortably mid-band; net income payout 35.9%. Spikes to 76.6% (FY2015) and 65.8% (FY2022) were weak-CFO years, not policy. Net debt is a floor (current maturities may be excluded), which does not affect this rule.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy, short enough to still be fast
rules.note: XBRL shows 16 straight increases FY2010-FY2025 with no hold, and the series starts at FY2009, so it is window-limited. Prior research streak of 30 is plausible for Donaldson and is used; it sits exactly at the upper bound, meaning the policy is proven but the easy-acceleration phase is likely behind it.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF 262.6M (FY2020) -> 339.9M (FY2025). A narrow 1.0pp miss, and endpoint-sensitive: FY2020 was a strong CFO year and FY2023/FY2024 FCF was above 400M. Net income CAGR is 7.39% and EBITDA 6.82%, both above the dividend, so the miss is cash-conversion timing rather than an earnings shortfall - but the rule as written fails.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 ROIC 19.0%, and 17.8%-26.3% in every measurable year FY2010-FY2025 (FY2018's 15.6% is a TCJA tax artefact; FY2009 is null for missing debt facts). Strong-tier, and consistent - the best number in this record.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Net debt 490.8M / EBITDA 594.9M. Has sat in a 0.48x-1.07x band since FY2015. Treat 0.83x as a floor: debtCur used ShortTermBorrowings only and may exclude current maturities of long-term debt, but the headroom to 2.5x is far too wide for that to matter.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.value: replacement-filter aftermarket on a large installed base
rules.note: Filters are spec'd into engines and industrial systems at OEM design-in, then replaced on a service interval for the life of the equipment; the aftermarket is roughly two-thirds of sales, is bought by fleet and plant maintenance buyers who will not risk a non-spec part on a $400k machine, and the filter is a trivial share of the owner's cost. That is a durable switching-cost mechanism, corroborated by the 19-23% ROIC and 9.2% FCF margin, not price competition.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: DPS rose 0.80 -> 0.84 -> 0.86 straight through COVID, and PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock rose every single year of the window. 2008-09 is outside the XBRL window and cannot be tested from this data.

analysis.assessment: Donaldson is a high-quality compounder that fails the entry math rather than the business test: 19.0% ROIC, 0.83x net debt/EBITDA, a 38.8% FCF payout and 16 data-confirmed (likely ~30 actual) years of unbroken increases, all intact. But the snowball starts at a 1.32% yield on 1.14 of FY2025 dividends against an $86.33 price and compounds at only 6.30% over five years, so the yield-on-cost is still under 2.5% a decade out - the combination of a sub-band yield and sub-8% growth is what caps this at candidate. There is genuine runway: the payout could roughly double before hitting the 60% ceiling, 3-yr DPS growth has re-accelerated to 8.20%, and FY2026 is running at a >=1.20 rate (FMP ttm 1.24 implies a Q4 raise to roughly 0.34). The thing most likely to break it is not the dividend but capital allocation: 331.5M of FY2025 buybacks is 2.5x the 131.9M dividend, and management has consistently chosen shrinking the share count over accelerating the payout, so the dividend stays a slow 6-8% grower unless that priority changes. Watch FCF conversion too - FY2022 (167.3M) and FY2025 (339.9M, down from 406.9M) show working-capital swings big enough to push payout above 60% in a bad year.

screenFields.streakSource: research; data confirms 16 years (FY2010-FY2025, window-limited - XBRL begins FY2009)
screenFields.payoutBasis: dividends / free cash flow (FY2025: 131.9M / 339.9M); net income basis 35.9%

estimateCorrections.why: Filed split-adjusted DPS 0.84 (FY2020) -> 1.14 (FY2025) is a 6.30% CAGR, 2.7pp below the estimate. The 9% guess looks like an extrapolation of the older 2011-2014 era (15-20% raises) or of the recent 3-yr rate of 8.20%; the actual five-year window includes the deliberately small FY2020 (+4.8%) and FY2021 (+2.4%) COVID-era raises. This flips rule 3 from pass to fail.

FY2025 dividends 131.9M against FCF 339.9M (CFO 418.8M less capex 78.9M) is 38.8%, 8.8pp above the estimate. The 30% figure would match FY2024 (30.2%) or FY2021 (31.3%); FY2025 FCF fell from 406.9M while dividends rose to 131.9M. Rule 4 still passes, but with less headroom than assumed.

No change to the screen value, but the basis is now explicit: only 16 consecutive increases (FY2010-FY2025) are derivable, and the data window starts at FY2009 so the measured streak is window-limited. The 30 is retained from prior research as plausible and is flagged as research-sourced rather than data-confirmed.

analysis.moat: Filtration with a large replacement-filter aftermarket attached to an installed base that was spec'd in at OEM design-in, so the recurring filter sale is protected by switching cost and warranty risk rather than price.
strengths: ROIC 19.0% in FY2025 and 17.8-26.3% in every measurable year since FY2010 - genuinely capital-light for an industrial.
Payout 38.8% of FCF and 35.9% of net income: the dividend could roughly double before stressing the 60% ceiling.
Net debt/EBITDA 0.83x, in a 0.48-1.07x band since FY2015; the balance sheet is not competing for the dividend.
No cut and no hold anywhere in the 16-year window, including FY2020 and FY2021 - the promise held through COVID.
3-yr DPS growth of 8.20% versus 5.46% over 10 years: the raise rate is re-accelerating, and FY2026 is already at a >=1.20 run-rate.
risks: 1.32% starting yield (1.44% on ttm 1.24) is well below the 1.5-4.0% usable band - the snowball starts very small.
6.30% 5-yr DPS CAGR misses the 8% bar; at that rate yield-on-cost is still under 2.5% in ten years.
5-yr FCF CAGR of 5.30% lags the 6.30% dividend growth, so the payout ratio has been drifting up (30.2% in FY2024 to 38.8% in FY2025).
FY2025 buybacks of 331.5M are 2.5x the 131.9M of dividends; management's revealed preference is share count over payout, which caps dividend acceleration.
FCF is working-capital volatile (167.3M in FY2022 against 426.0M in FY2023); a repeat of FY2022 with today's dividend would put payout near 79%.
Reported net debt of 490.8M may exclude current maturities of long-term debt (debtCur = ShortTermBorrowings only), so 0.83x is a floor - immaterial at this leverage but worth noting.
Streak at the top of the 10-30 band: a 30-year record signals a mature, institutionalised policy, not one about to speed up.
analysis.sectorNote: Donaldson is a straightforward industrial manufacturer, so all ten rules apply as written with no sector substitution: FCF = CFO - capex is the right payout denominator (FCF is positive in all 17 years and averages ~9% of revenue), net debt/EBITDA is meaningful, and ROIC on equity + total debt - cash is economically sensible for an asset-light filtration business. The only judgement calls are non-sectoral: rule 5's streak is window-limited by the XBRL start (FY2009) and takes the prior research figure of 30, and rule 6 was assessed on FCF as specified - on net income (7.39% CAGR) or EBITDA (6.82%) it would pass, and that divergence is noted rather than used to override the rule.

stocks.m: Convenience stores with prepared-food kitchen economics in towns too small to support a second modern competitor - the rural footprint blocks entry and the pizza/kitchen margin is what a fuel-led rival cannot replicate.

normalised.dpsMethod: FY2009-FY2014: filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid (10-K/10-K/A, ~364-day durations). FY2015-FY2023: filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (10-K, ~364-365 day durations). FY2024: no annual fact filed; summed the quarterly declared rates inside the May-2023/Apr-2024 fiscal year (Q1 0.43, Q2 0.43 implied from 0.86 cumulative, Q3 0.43 implied from 1.29 cumulative) and applied 4x the latest quarterly rate for the missing Q4 => 4 x 0.43 = 1.72. FY2025-FY2026: no DPS facts at all; derived by bracketing PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic against DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic. NO split adjustment applied to any year.

specials.note: No special dividends found. splitFacts is empty and no year shows filed DPS materially ABOVE divPaid/sharesBasic - filed DPS runs 1-3% above cash-paid-per-share and 0-1.5% below declared-per-share, the normal declared-vs-paid lag for a company that raises its rate every June (fiscal Q1). The one large jump, FY2011 DPS 0.34 -> 0.505 (+48.5%), is a genuine regular-rate increase (2010 Couche-Tard hostile-bid defense), not a special: FY2011 divPaid/sharesBasic is 0.4840, within 4.2% of the filed 0.505, whereas a special would leave the regular rate far below cash paid.

issues: NO SPLIT ADJUSTMENT APPLIED - splitFacts is empty and the evidence rules out a split anywhere in the window. The only step-change in sharesBasic is FY2010 50,899,370 -> FY2011 42,284,664 (-17%), explained by the $501,026,000 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock in FY2011 (Dutch-auction self-tender during the Couche-Tard hostile bid). A split would RAISE the share count, not cut it. Independently, divPaid/sharesBasic is self-consistent with the filed DPS in every year (max deviation 4.2%, FY2011), so no year sits on a different share basis. splitAdjustments.yearsAdjusted is empty: 0 years adjusted.

FY2011 is the only year where the cross-check deviates by more than ~3%: filed DPS 0.505 vs divPaid/sharesBasic 0.4840 (-4.2%). Judgement: buyback timing (shares fell through the year while the weighted-average denominator lags), not a special and not a basis error. Kept the filed 0.505.

MIXED DPS TAG BASIS: FY2009-FY2014 come from CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid (cash paid) while FY2015-FY2023 come from CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared. Because the rate is raised every June (fiscal Q1), the cash-paid measure runs about one quarter behind declared, so FY2009-FY2014 are slightly conservative relative to later years. No overlap year exists to calibrate the two tags. This is the largest source of imprecision in gMax.

FY2024 DPS (1.72) is NOT a filed annual fact. Only three quarterly declared facts exist for FY2024 (Q1 0.43; Q2 cumulative 0.86 -> 0.43; Q3 cumulative 1.29 -> 0.43); Q4 is missing (DPS tags stop after the FY2024 Q3 10-Q). Applied rule (b): 4 x latest quarterly rate 0.43 = 1.72. Corroborated by DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic = 1.7402 (+1.2%) and PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic = 1.6930 (-1.6%).

FY2025 DPS (2.00) and FY2026 DPS (2.28) are NOT filed - no DPS fact of any kind exists after 2024-01-31. Derived by bracketing each year between two per-share measures that straddle the filed rate: FY2025 PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic = 1.9482 and DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic = 2.0310 -> midpoint 1.9896, taken as 2.0000 ($0.50/qtr); FY2026 PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic = 2.2430 and DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic = 2.3135 -> midpoint 2.2782, taken as 2.2800 ($0.57/qtr). The straddle is validated on the nine years where the filed value is known: DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic averages ~+0.4% above filed and PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic ~-2.0% below it, in every year without exception. Independent corroboration: FMP ttmDividend 2.36 as of 2026-09-17 equals 3 x 0.57 + 0.65 (three FY2026-rate payments plus one post-raise payment), which only reconciles if the FY2026 quarterly rate was 0.57. These two years remain judgement values, not filed values - hence confidence medium, not high.

EBITDA is derived, not filed: no operating-income tag exists in the extract. Used EBITDA = (pretax + InterestExpense) + DepreciationAndAmortization. This treats non-operating other income/expense as operating and ignores capitalized interest (InterestCostsCapitalized, $3,189,000 in FY2026), so EBITDA and every netDebtToEbitda are approximations.

Pretax income is only filed for FY2009-FY2019 (tag stops at 2019-04-30). For FY2020-FY2026 pretax was reconstructed as NetIncomeLoss + IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit. Verified exact on overlap years (FY2018: 317,903 + (-103,466) = 214,437 = filed; FY2019: 203,886 + 59,516 = 263,402 = filed).

FY2018 effective tax rate is NEGATIVE (-48.25%: IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit -$103,466,000 on $214,437,000 pretax - the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act remeasurement benefit). Applied the rule literally, so (1 - t) = 1.4825 and FY2018 ROIC of 15.58% is overstated; it is the highest ROIC in the series purely because of a one-off tax credit. I did not substitute the 21% fallback because the rate WAS derivable.

FY2009 has no sharesBasic, debtLT, debtCur or assets in the table (those tags start 2010-04-30), so FY2009 netDebt, netDebtToEbitda, roic and sharesBasic are null and no FY2009 per-share cross-check was possible.

Revenue is null for FY2009-FY2015. The Revenues tag starts 2016-04-30 and the table carries no earlier revenue; SalesRevenueNet exists in families (2009-2017, 9 points) but its series was not included in the extract, so I did not invent values. fcfMargin is only computable from FY2016 onward.

FCF was NEGATIVE in FY2013 (-$18,973,000), FY2015 (-$12,089,000) and FY2018 (-$157,624,000) - heavy new-store/acquisition build years - so payoutFcf is null for those three years per the rule. FY2014 payoutFcf is 4.9023 (490%) because FCF was barely positive at $5,527,000; arithmetically correct but meaningless as a payout ratio.
FY2017 payoutFcf 1.4203 (142%) and FY2020 payoutFcf 0.7033 (70%) are real but capex-cycle artifacts, not dividend stress. Over FY2021-FY2026 payoutFcf sits in an 11-17% band.

Two divPaid tags disagree by 2-4% in most years (PaymentsOfDividends = cash out the door; DividendsCommonStock = declared). I used the primary tag PaymentsOfDividends for fin.divPaid and all payout ratios, and used DividendsCommonStock only as the upper bracket in the FY2025/FY2026 DPS derivation. Using the other tag would raise every payout ratio by roughly 3%.

priorEstimates were materially off and are replaced: growth5y guessed 13% (actual 5-yr DPS CAGR 11.55%), streak guessed 26 years (only 17 consecutive increases are observable in this window, FY2010-FY2026; the streak runs to the start of the data so it may extend earlier - windowLimited is true, and the 26-year claim is neither confirmed nor refuted here), payoutPctFcf guessed 20% (actual FY2026 11.5%).

FY2026 revenue-based fcfMargin of 4.11% is structurally low because the Revenues tag is gross fuel revenue including motor-fuel excise/pass-through economics; it is not comparable to a non-fuel retailer's margin.

normalised.notes: Casey's General Stores, FYE April 30, so FY2026 = year ended 2026-04-30 (already filed). 18 fiscal years of cash-flow data (FY2009-FY2026) and 18 derivable DPS years. No stock split and no special dividend anywhere in the window; splitAdjustments is deliberately empty and the FY2011 share-count drop is a $501M self-tender, not a split. Regular DPS rises every single year from $0.30 (FY2009) to $2.28 (FY2026) - 17 unbroken increases inside the data, no cut and no hold, including through FY2020/FY2021. The dividend shape is a single annual raise declared each June (fiscal Q1), which is why declared-per-share runs about one quarter ahead of cash-paid-per-share every year. Growth is accelerating rather than decaying: 9.99% over 10 years, 11.55% over 5, 14.47% over 3 - the company moved from ~8-9% raises (FY2015-FY2022) to 13-16% raises (FY2024-FY2026) as FCF inflected. Coverage is not the binding constraint: FY2026 FCF of $722M covers the $83M dividend 8.7x (11.5% of FCF, 11.6% of net income), FCF compounded 14.7%/yr over 5 years, and net debt/EBITDA fell back to 1.29x in FY2026 after the FY2025 spike to 1.82x on the CEFCO acquisition. The real historical caveat is capex intensity - FCF was negative in three of eighteen years (FY2013, FY2015, FY2018) on build-outs, so the low payout ratio is better read as a buffer against the next build cycle than as free headroom. FY2025 and FY2026 DPS are derived, not filed, and are the main figures to re-verify once the FY2026 10-K DPS tags appear.

Used substitutes: FY2026 divPaid/sharesBasic 2.2430 and DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic 2.3135 bracket 2.28 with no per-share spike; live.ttmDividend 2.36 with live.regularDividendIfSpecial null. No evidence of a special. PASS with caveat (see issues).

issues.detail: The stated validation of the FY2025/FY2026 bracketing method is factually false. The record claims 'DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic averages ~+0.4% above filed and PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic ~-2.0% below it, in every year without exception.' Recomputed, DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic is BELOW the filed DPS in 5 of the 13 testable years: FY2011 -4.15%, FY2017 -0.07%, FY2018 -0.58%, FY2019 -0.26%, FY2020 -0.44%. So the 'upper bracket' is not an upper bracket in ~38% of years and the straddle is not validated as claimed. The mean of the DividendsCommonStock/share bias over FY2012-FY2023 is only about +0.22%, not +0.4%. The derived values 2.00 and 2.28 still survive (they equal clean quarterly rates 0.50 and 0.57 and reconcile with live.ttmDividend 2.36 = 3x0.57 + 0.65), so this is a justification defect, not a value defect.
issues.suggested: Keep dps 2.00 / 2.28 but rewrite the issue text: 'DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic runs on average +0.22% vs filed DPS but is below filed in 5 of 13 testable years (FY2011, FY2017-FY2020), so it is not a strict upper bound; the straddle is indicative, not proven.'

issues.detail: The derivation rules' fallback (c) is explicitly 'divPaid / weighted basic shares as the derived series'. The record instead invented a midpoint-of-two-tags method plus a round-to-clean-quarterly-rate step. Applying rule (c) literally gives FY2025 = 72,309,000/37,116,152 = 1.9482 and FY2026 = 83,136,000/37,065,319 = 2.2430, i.e. the record sits +2.66% and +1.65% above the rule-(c) values. Both are within the 5% cross-check tolerance and the record's values are better estimates of the declared rate, but the method deviates from the stated ladder and should be labelled as such.
issues.suggested: Either set dps[2025]=1.9482 / dps[2026]=2.2430 with basis 'derived-from-cash' per rule (c), or keep 2.00/2.28 and change basis to 'derived-judgement (rounded to implied quarterly rate)' so it is not mistaken for the rule-(c) series. Rule-(c) values would give g3 = (2.2430/1.52)^(1/3)-1 = 13.83%, g5 = 11.19%, g10 = 9.81%.

issues.detail: The claimed direction of the FY2009-FY2014 bias is contradicted by the raw data. The record says the CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid years 'run about one quarter behind declared' and are therefore 'slightly conservative'. Recomputed, the FY2012-FY2014 CashPaid values match DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic (the declared measure) to within 0.06% (FY2012 0.600 vs 0.6002; FY2013 0.660 vs 0.6604; FY2014 0.720 vs 0.7203) and sit 2.2-2.4% ABOVE PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic. Those values are effectively on the declared basis despite the tag name. FY2010 is the exception: 0.34 equals PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic 0.3400 exactly, i.e. genuinely cash-paid. So the basis is mixed WITHIN the early block, not cleanly one-quarter-lagged, and gMax is not biased in the direction claimed.
issues.suggested: Replace with: 'FY2012-FY2014 CashPaid-tag values reconcile to DividendsCommonStock/shares within 0.06%, i.e. they are on the declared basis despite the tag name; FY2010 reconciles exactly to PaymentsOfDividends/shares (true cash basis). The early block is internally mixed, but the maximum implied distortion is ~2.4% in one or two years, so gMax 12.67% is not materially biased. FY2009 remains uncheckable (no sharesBasic).'

issues.detail: basis is labelled 'summed-quarters' but only three quarterly facts exist inside FY2024 (Q1 0.43; Q2 cumulative 0.86; Q3 cumulative 1.29) and Q4 was extrapolated as 4x the latest rate. The label hides an extrapolation and makes FY2024 look filed-quarter-complete. The VALUE 1.72 is correct under rule (b) and is bracketed by PaymentsOfDividends/shares 1.6930 (-1.6%) and DividendsCommonStock/shares 1.7402 (+1.2%).
issues.suggested: basis: "4x-latest-quarter" (value unchanged at 1.72)

issues.detail: Check 7 as specified cannot be executed: dpsAllFacts contains no DPS fact with an end date after 2024-01-31, so neither FY2025 nor FY2026 quarterly rates are verifiable from filed facts. The record's regularity argument for the latest DPS rests on live.ttmDividend 2.36 and an assumed post-year raise to 0.65. That arithmetic does hold (3 x 0.57 + 0.65 = 2.36) and live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null, but no filed quarterly fact confirms the 0.57 rate. Flagging because the latest two data points - the ones that drive g3, latest.dps and the streak endpoint - are unverifiable from filings.
issues.suggested: Add to issues: 'Check 7 (latest DPS regular vs special from quarterly facts) is UNRUNNABLE - no DPS fact of any tag exists after 2024-01-31. Regularity is inferred from live.ttmDividend 2.36 and the per-share cash bracket only; re-verify when the FY2026 10-K DPS tags appear.' Consider confidence 'low' rather than 'medium' for dps[2025]/dps[2026] specifically.

issues.detail: Two minor factual slips. (a) The FY2011 deviation is stated as -4.2%; recomputed it is -4.15% measuring cash/share against filed (0.4840 vs 0.505) or +4.33% measuring filed against cash/share - immaterial, but the record also calls FY2011 'the only year where the cross-check deviates by more than ~3%' which is true only against PaymentsOfDividends; FY2020 (+2.94%), FY2019 (+2.78%) and FY2015 (+2.72%) sit just under the line. (b) 'Two divPaid tags disagree by 2-4% in most years' is wrong for FY2011 and FY2012, where PaymentsOfDividends and DividendsCommonStock are byte-identical (20,467,000 and 22,849,000); the disagreement starts in FY2013.
issues.suggested: (a) '-4.15%'; (b) 'The two divPaid tags are identical in FY2011-FY2012 and diverge by 2-4% from FY2013 onward.'

issues.detail: yearsCovered is reported as 18 while every CAGR in the record (correctly) uses 17 compounding periods between FY2009 and FY2026. 18 is the count of data points, not the span. Harmless internally but invites a downstream consumer to recompute gMax over 18 years, which would give 11.93% instead of 12.67%.
issues.suggested: Either yearsCovered: 17 (compounding periods, matching gMax) or rename the field so the 18-point/17-period distinction is explicit.

issues.detail: The note asserts 'no year shows filed DPS materially ABOVE divPaid/sharesBasic' and then immediately concedes FY2011 sits 4.2% above it - the assertion and the evidence in the same field contradict each other. The conclusion (FY2011 is a genuine rate increase, not a special) is nonetheless supported: the FY2011 gap is fully explained by the weighted-average denominator lagging the 501,026,000 self-tender (sharesOut fell to 37,966,709 while weighted basic was 42,284,664), and DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic equals PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic exactly in FY2011, so there is no declared-vs-paid wedge to attribute to a special.
issues.suggested: Reword to 'no year shows filed DPS materially above divPaid/sharesBasic except FY2011 (+4.2%), which is explained by the FY2011 self-tender share-count timing, not a special.'

checksRun: 1. Latest regular DPS 2.28 (FY2026, derived) vs live.ttmDividend 2.36 as of 2026-09-17: gap -3.4%, inside the ~10% band. Fully explained: TTM spans Nov-2025/Feb-2026/May-2026 payments at the FY2026 rate of $0.57 plus the Aug-2026 payment at a post-year-end raised rate. 3 x 0.57 + 0.65 = 2.36 exactly, implying a June-2026 raise to $0.65/qtr (+14.0%), consistent with the record's stated single-annual-raise-each-June pattern. live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null and CASY is not one of the four special-payers, so ttmDividend is the right comparator. No special contamination. PASS.

2. live.marketCap 21,795,886,100 / live.price 589 = 37,004,900 implied shares. vs record latest sharesBasic (FY2026) 37,065,319 = -0.16%; vs coverSharesOutstanding 36,960,167 (asOf 2026-09-02) = +0.12%. All three agree within 0.2%, far inside 15%. This independently corroborates the no-split conclusion: any unadjusted split in the window would show up as a multiple-of-2/3 mismatch here, and none exists. The FY2010->FY2011 50.9M->42.3M drop is a share-count DECREASE (self-tender), which a split cannot produce. PASS.

3. Implied regular yield = 2.28 / 589 = 0.387% (0.401% on the TTM 2.36, 0.441% on the new $0.65/qtr run-rate = $2.60). Inside the 0.2%-8% sanity band and economically coherent for a ~$21.8B low-payout compounder (payoutNi 11.6%, payoutFcf 11.5%). PASS.

4. 5-yr DPS CAGR 11.55% plausibility vs sector/size/moat: Casey's General Stores is a Consumer Cyclical convenience-store/fuel retailer, ~$17.6B revenue, ~$21.8B cap, priorEstimates flag 'graduated'. An 11.6% 5-yr dividend CAGR on an 11-13% payout ratio with 14.7% 5-yr FCF growth and 13.5% ROIC is internally and externally coherent - the raises are funded out of a widening FCF base, not leverage (net debt/EBITDA 1.29x). The acceleration (g10 9.99% -> g5 11.55% -> g3 14.47%) matches the real inside-store-margin/CEFCO-scale story and is confirmed by the independent June-2026 +14.0% raise implied by ttmDividend. Not a red flag. PASS.

5. Divergences vs priorEstimates: growth5y 13 vs actual 11.55; payoutPctFcf 20 vs actual 11.5; streak 26 vs 17-in-window. All three are named and reasoned in dataQuality.issues (last issue block) rather than silently overwritten. The g5 and payoutFcf divergences are arithmetically verified from the record's own series (recomputed: g5 11.55%, g10 9.99%, g3 14.47%, gMax 12.67% - all reproduce exactly). Explained. PASS with one warn on the streak field's downstream presentation.

6. Streak vs data window: 18 fiscal years of data (FY2009-FY2026), consecutiveIncreasesInData = 17 (FY2010 through FY2026), windowLimited = true, and the record explicitly declines to assert the 26-year claim. The streak does not exceed what the window can support. PASS.

Cross-check of DPS levels against the declared-rate ladder implied by live data: FY2024 1.72 = 4 x 0.43, FY2025 2.00 = 4 x 0.50, FY2026 2.28 = 4 x 0.57, FY2027 run-rate 2.60 = 4 x 0.65. Each step is a clean quarterly-rate multiple with raises of 16.3%/16.3%/14.0%, a coherent ladder with no missing or doubled year - a missed split or a mis-summed quarter would break the ladder.

Dividend-cash coherence: FY2026 divPaid 83,136,000 / sharesBasic 37,065,319 = 2.2430/sh, 1.6% below the derived declared 2.28, matching the record's stated ~-2.0% paid-vs-declared lag for a June raiser. Consistent.

issues.detail: FY2026 ended 2026-04-30 and today is 2026-09-20, so the FY2026 10-K is filed, yet the extract carries no DPS fact after 2024-01-31 and both FY2025 and FY2026 remain 'derived-from-cash'. External data does not refute the values - ttmDividend 2.36 reconciles only at a $0.57 FY2026 quarterly rate, and 83,136,000/37,065,319 = $2.2430 paid/sh brackets 2.28 from below exactly as the record predicts - but the basis label understates how verifiable these now are. Flagging because the record's own notes call these 'the main figures to re-verify' and the source to do so should already exist.
issues.suggested: Keep val 2.28 (FY2026) and 2.00 (FY2025) - both are corroborated to within 2% by two independent per-share measures and exactly by the ttmDividend decomposition 3 x 0.57 + 0.65 = 2.36. Re-pull CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared from the FY2026 10-K (filed ~June 2026) and promote basis to 'filed' if it returns 2.28/2.00; if the extract genuinely lacks the tag, leave basis as-is and keep confidence 'medium'.

issues.detail: The field reports 17 and correctly sets windowLimited=true, which satisfies the window test. The external-reality caveat is the opposite of the usual failure: Casey's real uninterrupted increase streak starts around FY2000, so a consumer reading streak=17 without reading windowLimited will UNDERSTATE the record by ~9 years and could mis-rank CASY against true dividend-aristocrat screens. The record is honest about this; the risk is in downstream display, not in the number.
issues.suggested: Keep 17. Ensure any consumer surfaces windowLimited=true alongside it, e.g. render as '17+ (data window starts FY2009; priorEstimates claim 26, unverified here)'. Do not silently substitute 26.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: Live marketCap 21,795,886,100 at $589 on 2026-09-17. Roughly 45% above the $15B line and 4.4x the ideal, so the easy-doubling phase is behind it; growth now has to come from CEFCO-style acquisition and inside-store mix, not from a small base.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: Latest regular annual DPS 2.28 / price 589 = 0.387%. Even on the post-June-2026 run-rate of $2.60 (4 x $0.65) it is only 0.44%. Roughly a quarter of the minimum band: this is a dividend-growth compounder, not an income holding, and the snowball starts from almost nothing.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr DPS CAGR FY2021 1.32 -> FY2026 2.28. Accelerating, not decaying: g10 9.99%, g5 11.55%, g3 14.47%, and the June-2026 raise implied by ttmDividend 2.36 (3 x 0.57 + 0.65) is +14.0%. Just short of the 12% 'strong' mark on the 5-yr measure; the 3-yr measure clears it comfortably.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2026 dividends 83.1M / FCF 721.6M = 11.52% (11.64% of net income); FY2021-FY2026 sits in an 11-17% band. Fails on the LOW side - the opposite of dividend stress. FCF covers the dividend 8.7x, which is deliberate: FCF was negative in FY2013, FY2015 and FY2018 on store build-outs, so the thin payout is a buffer against the next capex cycle rather than idle headroom.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: Data shows 17 unbroken increases FY2010-FY2026 running back to the first year of the XBRL window (FY2009), so the data streak is window-limited and is a floor, not the true length. priorEstimates.streak of 26 is plausible (Casey's has raised since roughly FY2000) and sits inside the 10-30 band, so I used 26 for the screen and flagged the source. Either figure passes.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF FY2021 362.8M -> FY2026 721.6M, +3.2pp ahead of the dividend, so the payout ratio has fallen while the dividend compounded at 11.6%. Net income grew faster still (312.9M -> 714.4M, 17.9%/yr). FCF endpoints are both solidly positive so no net-income substitution was needed.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2026 ROIC 13.45%, the best clean year in the series (FY2018's 15.58% is an artifact of the negative TCJA tax rate). But the series is a 9-15% band that hovers near the threshold - FY2019 9.33%, FY2025 10.74% on the CEFCO deal - so this is a pass with little margin, and EBITDA/operating income here is derived rather than filed.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: FY2026 net debt 1.909B / derived EBITDA 1.484B = 1.29x, down from the FY2025 CEFCO-acquisition peak of 1.82x. Worst year in the window is FY2018 at 2.58x. Comfortable, and deleveraging fast enough to fund the next deal without touching the dividend.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: Roughly half of Casey's ~2,900 stores sit in towns under 5,000 people, where one modern store saturates the demand and a second entrant cannot earn its cost of capital; on top of that footprint it runs the fifth-largest pizza chain in the US, giving 35-40% gross-margin prepared food that no fuel-led competitor can bolt on without the same kitchens, labour model and distribution centres. That is the opposite of price competition.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/FY2021; no cut anywhere in window
rules.note: FY2020 DPS 1.28 vs FY2019 1.16 and FY2021 1.32 - raised straight through COVID, when fuel volumes collapsed. No cut, no hold, no suspension anywhere FY2009-FY2026. 2008 is outside the XBRL window and is not assessable here. The rate rises once a year, each June (fiscal Q1).

analysis.assessment: Casey's is an excellent business wearing a dividend that barely exists: the 0.39% starting yield ($2.28 on a $589 price) means even 11.55% 5-yr dividend growth compounding for a decade only gets you to about 1.1% on cost, so the snowball here is total return, not income. The engine underneath is real - FY2026 FCF of $722M covers the $83M dividend 8.7x at an 11.5% payout, FCF compounded 14.74%/yr against the dividend's 11.55%, ROIC hit 13.45% and net debt/EBITDA fell back to 1.29x after the CEFCO deal - and the raises are accelerating (g10 9.99% -> g5 11.55% -> g3 14.47%, with a +14.0% June-2026 raise to $0.65/qtr implied by the $2.36 TTM). Two rules fail for structural reasons rather than weakness: at $21.8B market cap it is past the small-enough-to-grow line, and the payout is below the 20% floor, which is a capex buffer (FCF was negative in FY2013, FY2015 and FY2018 on build-outs) rather than caution. The most likely thing to break it is capital allocation, not the dividend: another large acquisition or a step-up in new-store capex turns FCF negative again as it did three times in eighteen years, and management would then fund raises out of a thinner base - the dividend itself would survive that, the 14% growth rate would not. Secondary risk: ROIC has only twice cleared 13% in the window, so the 12% rule passes on the strength of one good year.
analysis.moat: Convenience stores with prepared-food kitchen economics in towns too small to support a second modern competitor - the rural footprint blocks entry and the pizza/kitchen margin is what a fuel-led rival cannot replicate.
strengths: FY2026 FCF $721.6M covers the $83.1M dividend 8.7x; payout 11.5% of FCF and 11.6% of net income, the lowest in the 18-year window.
Dividend growth is accelerating, not fading: 9.99% (10-yr) -> 11.55% (5-yr) -> 14.47% (3-yr), with a +14.0% June-2026 raise to $0.65/qtr implied by the $2.36 TTM.
FCF grew 14.74%/yr over five years and net income 17.9%/yr, both faster than the dividend, so the payout ratio keeps falling while raises get bigger.
17 consecutive increases inside the data (likely ~26 in reality), raised straight through FY2020-FY2021 when fuel volumes collapsed.
Net debt/EBITDA 1.29x in FY2026, already back down from the 1.82x CEFCO peak; balance sheet is not competing with the shareholder.
risks: 0.39% starting yield: a decade of 11.5% growth still leaves roughly 1.1% yield on cost, so nearly all the return must come from the multiple and earnings.
$21.8B market cap is 45% past the small-enough-to-grow line; incremental growth now depends on acquisitions like CEFCO rather than a small base.
Capex intensity - FCF was negative in FY2013, FY2015 and FY2018 on store build-outs, and a new build or deal cycle would compress the FCF base the raises are funded from.
ROIC is a 9-15% band that only just clears the 12% rule in FY2026 (13.45%); FY2019 was 9.33% and FY2025 10.74%. FY2018's 15.58% is a negative-tax-rate artifact, not a real high.
Fuel-price exposure: revenue is gross of motor-fuel pass-through, so reported margins and EBITDA swing with fuel spreads that management does not control.

FY2025 and FY2026 DPS ($2.00 and $2.28) are derived from cash-paid and declared per-share brackets, not filed DPS tags - no DPS fact exists after 2024-01-31, so the two most recent points, which drive g3 and the latest yield, need re-verification against the FY2026 10-K.
analysis.sectorNote: Standard operating-company rules apply - CASY is a convenience-store/fuel retailer, not a REIT, insurer or regulated utility, so rule 4 was read on dividends/FCF and rule 8 on net debt/EBITDA as written. The one model-specific caveat is rule 4's 20% floor: for a capex-heavy retailer that self-funds new stores and distribution centres, a sub-20% payout reads as deliberate reinvestment capacity, not as a failed test - FCF turned negative in three of eighteen years, and the thin payout is what let the dividend rise through those years untouched. Rule 7's ROIC also uses a derived EBIT (no operating-income tag is filed), so the 13.45% carries approximation error.

screenFields.streakSource: research; data confirms 17 years (FY2010-FY2026, window-limited at the FY2009 start of XBRL)

estimateCorrections.why: Prior estimate was 8.5pp too high. FY2026 dividends paid 83.1M against FCF 721.6M is 11.5%, and the FY2021-FY2026 range is 11-17% - the dividend has never approached 20% of FCF in the recent cycle. The 20% figure matches the older capex-light years, not today.

Prior 13% overstated the 5-yr CAGR by 1.45pp. Actual FY2021 1.32 -> FY2026 2.28 compounds at 11.55%. The 13% guess is closer to the 3-yr rate (14.47%) - growth accelerated late in the window, so a 3-yr impression was being applied to a 5-yr field. Below the 3pp materiality bar but corrected because the screen displays it directly.

Kept at 26 but the source changed. SEC data confirms only 17 consecutive increases (FY2010-FY2026), and that streak runs back to the first year of the XBRL window, so it is a floor rather than the true count. 26 is retained from prior research as plausible and inside the 10-30 band; streakSource now says the data confirms 17.
